concepts.name: Subatomic particles (electron, proton, neutron)
concepts.explanation: Properties of electrons, protons and neutrons including relative mass, relative charge and typical location within the atom.

concepts.name: Atomic number (Z), mass number (A) and isotopes
concepts.explanation: Definition and notation of atomic number and mass number; concept of isotopes with hydrogen and carbon as specific examples and how isotopes differ in nucleon number.

concepts.name: Relative atomic mass (Ar) and the 12C scale
concepts.explanation: Meaning of relative atomic mass, how Ar is defined relative to the carbon-12 scale and its use as a comparative atomic mass measure.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry for determining relative atomic mass
concepts.explanation: Use of the mass spectrometer to measure isotopic masses and abundances and thereby determine relative atomic masses.

concepts.name: Rutherford alpha-particle scattering experiment and the nuclear model
concepts.explanation: The alpha-particle scattering experiment and its interpretation leading to the conclusion that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus.
concepts.broader_concept: Historical experiments leading to nuclear model

concepts.name: Bohr model of the atom
concepts.explanation: Bohr's model describing quantized electron orbits and how it improved understanding of atomic spectra and electron energy levels (outline level).

concepts.name: Periodic table organization and trends
concepts.explanation: The periodic table as an arrangement of elements that reveals trends in physical and chemical properties across periods and down groups.

concepts.name: Characteristic properties of main periodic groups
concepts.explanation: Principal resemblances and typical properties of elements in the main groups: alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, halogens and noble gases.

concepts.name: Reaction of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) with water
concepts.explanation: Demonstration experiment and observation of how lithium, sodium and potassium react with water, illustrating group reactivity trends.

concepts.name: Mendeleev's periodic table compared with the modern periodic table
concepts.explanation: Mendeleev's arrangement of elements by relative atomic mass, his predictive use of gaps, and the differences between his table and the modern table ordered by atomic number.
concepts.broader_concept: History and development of the periodic table

concepts.name: Historical development of atomic theory (Dalton, Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr) - outline
concepts.explanation: A brief outline of key historical contributions to atomic theory: Dalton's atomic theory, Thomson's identification of the electron, Rutherford's nuclear model and Bohr's model (principles only).

concepts.name: Particle model of matter: atoms, molecules and ions
concepts.explanation: The concept that matter is composed of discrete particles which may be atoms, molecules or ions and how this underpins chemical behavior.

concepts.name: Law of conservation of mass in relation to atomic theory
concepts.explanation: The law that mass is conserved in chemical reactions and its explanation using the concept of atoms being neither created nor destroyed in ordinary chemical processes.

concepts.name: Electronic energy levels in atoms
concepts.explanation: Discrete main energy levels (shells) in atoms and the allowed numbers of electrons in each main energy level for elements 1–20.

concepts.name: Electronic configuration and classification by outer electrons (first 20 elements)
concepts.explanation: Writing electron arrangements for elements 1–20 and using number of outer (valence) electrons to classify elements into groups and predict simple chemical behaviour.

concepts.name: Octet rule and valency
concepts.explanation: The tendency of atoms to attain a noble-gas electron configuration (octet) and using this to explain valency and simple bonding, including known limitations.

concepts.name: Ionic bonding and sodium chloride lattice
concepts.explanation: Formation of positive and negative ions by electron transfer, representation by dot-and-cross diagrams, structure of the NaCl ionic lattice and characteristic properties of ionic substances.

concepts.name: Predicting simple compound formulas using electron arrangements
concepts.explanation: Using the octet rule/electron transfer ideas to predict formulas of simple binary compounds (first 36 elements excluding d-block) and common hydroxides and carbonates.

concepts.name: Atomic (covalent) radii and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: Definition of covalent (atomic) radius and explanations for general trends in covalent radii down a group and across a period for main-group elements.

concepts.name: Screening effect, nuclear charge and trends in group reactivity (groups I and VII)
concepts.explanation: How effective nuclear charge and electron shielding (screening) influence atomic properties and thereby explain trends in chemical reactivity for Group 1 (alkali metals) and Group 7 (halogens).

concepts.name: Flame tests for metal identification (mandatory experiment 1.1)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative test using characteristic flame colours to identify certain metal ions (Li, Na, K, Ba, Sr and Cu) and relate observed colours to electronic transitions.

concepts.name: Types of radioactivity: alpha, beta and gamma radiation
concepts.explanation: Nature (particle or photon) and relative penetrating ability of alpha (α), beta (β) and gamma (γ) radiation, with illustrative example emitters.

concepts.name: Radioisotopes and their applications
concepts.explanation: Concept of radioisotopes and selected applications such as radiocarbon (14C) dating, 60Co in cancer treatment, and food irradiation.

concepts.name: Half-life (conceptual/non-mathematical)
concepts.explanation: The qualitative idea of half-life as the time required for half the atoms in a sample of a radioisotope to decay (no calculations required).

concepts.name: Oxidation and reduction as electron transfer
concepts.explanation: Definition of oxidation (loss of electrons) and reduction (gain of electrons), identification of oxidising and reducing agents with simple examples.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrochemical series (metals ordered by ease of oxidation)
concepts.explanation: The electrochemical series as an ordered list of metals according to their tendency to be oxidised (used to predict displacement and related behaviours).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis: CuSO4 with copper electrodes and acidified water with inert electrodes (mandatory)
concepts.explanation: Practical electrolysis procedures illustrating ion migration and electrode reactions: copper sulfate with copper electrodes and electrolysis of acidified water with inert electrodes (half-equations at electrodes).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Halogens as oxidising agents (redox reactions with halides, Fe2+, sulfites)
concepts.explanation: Reactivity of halogens as oxidants illustrated by their reactions with halide ions, iron(II) and sulfite ions (qualitative redox behaviour and observations).

concepts.name: Metal displacement reactions (examples: Zn with Cu2+, Mg with Cu2+)
concepts.explanation: Single displacement redox reactions where a more active metal displaces a less active metal ion from solution; illustrative examples and connection to the electrochemical series.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Covalent bond (sharing of electron pairs)
concepts.explanation: Chemical bond formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of electrons, creating a molecule.

concepts.name: Single, double and triple covalent bonds
concepts.explanation: Types of covalent bonds distinguished by the number of shared electron pairs (one, two, or three), affecting bond length and strength.

concepts.name: Polar vs non-polar covalent bonds
concepts.explanation: Classification of covalent bonds by whether electrons are shared unequally (polar, resulting in a dipole) or equally (non-polar), typically due to differences in electronegativity.

concepts.name: Dot-and-cross (Lewis) diagrams for covalent bonds
concepts.explanation: Representation method using dots and crosses to show valence electrons, shared pairs (bonds) and lone pairs in covalent molecules.

concepts.name: Physical characteristics of covalent substances
concepts.explanation: Typical properties of covalent (molecular) substances — e.g., generally low melting and boiling points, poor electrical conductivity in solid and molten states, and varied solubility depending on polarity.

concepts.name: Molecules and molecular size
concepts.explanation: Definition of a molecule as a discrete group of bonded atoms and the concept that molecules are extremely small (minute) compared to macroscopic objects.

concepts.name: Polarity test using charged plastic rod
concepts.explanation: Practical test where a charged plastic rod is brought near a liquid to observe attraction/repulsion or induced motion, indicating the liquid's polarity.

concepts.name: Solubility tests to distinguish ionic and covalent substances
concepts.explanation: Experimental procedure of testing substances in polar and non-polar solvents to assess solubility patterns, helping distinguish ionic compounds from molecular covalent substances.

concepts.name: Uses of common materials (e.g., salt tablets)
concepts.explanation: Application-focused concept: identifying everyday uses of materials (for example, salt tablets used to replace salts lost by sweating) and relating uses to material properties.

concepts.name: Classification of materials
concepts.explanation: Systematic grouping of everyday materials into categories (metals, polymers, ceramics, composites) with characteristic properties and typical uses.

concepts.name: Metals (properties and everyday examples)
concepts.explanation: The class of materials characterized by electrical and thermal conductivity, malleability, ductility and metallic luster; identify common examples and uses (e.g., copper wiring, aluminum foil).

concepts.name: Polymers (properties and everyday examples)
concepts.explanation: Materials made of long-chain macromolecules with properties such as low density and chemical resistance; identify common examples and uses (e.g., polyethylene bags, PVC pipes).

concepts.name: Ceramics (properties and everyday examples)
concepts.explanation: Inorganic, non-metallic materials often hard, brittle, and heat-resistant; identify common examples and uses (e.g., pottery, porcelain, bricks).

concepts.name: Composites (properties and everyday examples)
concepts.explanation: Engineered materials combining two or more constituent materials to obtain improved properties (e.g., fiberglass, carbon-fiber composites in sports equipment), with emphasis on constituent roles and applications.

concepts.name: Electronegativity and its periodic variation
concepts.explanation: Definition of electronegativity and explanation of general trends in electronegativity across a period and down a group in the periodic table.

concepts.name: Electronegativity differences and bond polarity
concepts.explanation: How differences in electronegativity between bonded atoms produce bond dipoles and determine whether a covalent bond is polar or nonpolar.

concepts.name: Prediction of bond type using electronegativity differences
concepts.explanation: Using the magnitude of electronegativity differences to classify bonds as ionic, polar covalent, or nonpolar covalent and predict bonding character.

concepts.name: Shapes of simple molecules (molecular geometry using models)
concepts.explanation: Recognition and illustration of the shapes of simple molecules using physical models or balloons to represent molecular geometry.

concepts.name: Intermolecular forces
concepts.explanation: Understanding the forces acting between molecules (intermolecular interactions) and their influence on physical properties.

concepts.name: Qualitative tests for common anions in aqueous solution: chloride, carbonate, nitrate, sulfate
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedures for identifying chloride, carbonate, nitrate and sulfate anions in aqueous solutions using standard qualitative tests.

concepts.name: The Mole and Avogadro Constant
concepts.explanation: Definition of the mole as the SI unit for amount of substance containing Avogadro's number of particles; understanding Avogadro constant and its role in counting atoms/molecules.

concepts.name: Molar Mass and Relative Molecular Mass (Mr)
concepts.explanation: Calculation and use of molar mass and relative molecular mass (Mr) from relative atomic masses to convert between moles and mass.

concepts.name: Conversions: Moles ↔ Masses, Volumes, Number of Particles
concepts.explanation: Procedures to convert between amount of substance (moles) and grams, litres (of gases at given conditions) and number of particles using molar mass, molar volume and Avogadro's number.

concepts.name: Empirical Formula Determination from Percentage Composition
concepts.explanation: Method to calculate an empirical formula using percentage composition by mass data and mole ratios.

concepts.name: Molecular Formula Calculation from Empirical Formula and Mr
concepts.explanation: Procedure to determine the molecular formula by relating empirical formula mass to the compound's relative molecular mass (examples include glucose and urea).

concepts.name: Percentage Composition by Mass
concepts.explanation: Calculating the mass percent of each element in a compound and using it in further stoichiometric analyses.

concepts.name: Balancing Chemical Equations
concepts.explanation: Techniques for writing and balancing chemical equations to conserve atoms and charge before quantitative calculations.

concepts.name: Stoichiometric Calculations from Balanced Equations
concepts.explanation: Use of balanced chemical equations and the mole concept to calculate masses and volumes of reactants and products (including provided balanced equations).

concepts.name: Standard Temperature and Pressure (s.t.p.) and Molar Volume
concepts.explanation: Definition of standard temperature and pressure and the molar volume of an ideal gas at s.t.p., used in gas calculations.

concepts.name: Combined Gas Law (P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2)
concepts.explanation: Relationship combining Boyle's and Charles's laws to relate pressure, volume and temperature between two states of a gas for fixed mass.

concepts.name: Boyle's Law
concepts.explanation: Inverse relationship between pressure and volume of a fixed amount of gas at constant temperature (P ∝ 1/V).

concepts.name: Charles's Law
concepts.explanation: Direct relationship between volume and temperature of a fixed amount of gas at constant pressure (V ∝ T, with temperature in K).

concepts.name: Correction of Gas Volumes to s.t.p. (units and calculations)
concepts.explanation: Procedures for correcting measured gas volumes to standard temperature and pressure using gas laws, including appropriate units (Pa, cm3, K).

concepts.name: States of Matter: Particle Motion in Solids, Liquids and Gases
concepts.explanation: Qualitative description of how particle motion and arrangement differ in solids, liquids and gases and how these differences explain macroscopic properties.

concepts.name: Diffusion (Qualitative Examples)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative concept of diffusion in gases and liquids with classroom demonstrations (e.g., NH3 and HCl, ink in water, smoke in air); Graham's law not required.

concepts.name: Structural Formulas
concepts.explanation: Representation of molecules using structural formulas to show bonding arrangement of atoms in simple molecules.

concepts.name: Laboratory Determination of Relative Molecular Mass of a Volatile Liquid
concepts.explanation: Mandatory experiment: determining the relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid using methods such as displacement into a conical flask or gas syringe and gas laws.

concepts.name: Acid-base titration
concepts.explanation: A quantitative titrimetric method where a solution of known concentration (titrant) is reacted with an acid or base of unknown concentration to determine its molarity, using an indicator or pH endpoint.

concepts.name: Standardisation of an acid solution (using a primary standard)
concepts.explanation: Procedure to determine the exact concentration of an acid solution by titration against a primary standard base (e.g., sodium carbonate) with known purity and mass.
concepts.broader_concept: Preparation and standardisation of standard solutions

concepts.name: Primary standard
concepts.explanation: A highly pure, stable substance used to prepare a solution of accurately known concentration because it can be weighed directly and dissolved to give a standard solution (e.g., anhydrous sodium carbonate for acid standardisation).

concepts.name: Preparation of a standard solution (sodium carbonate)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure for accurately weighing a primary standard (sodium carbonate), dissolving it, and diluting to a known volume to make a standard solution of known molarity.
concepts.broader_concept: Preparation and standardisation of standard solutions

concepts.name: Standard solution
concepts.explanation: A solution whose concentration is accurately known, either by preparation from a primary standard or by standardisation (used as titrant or reference in volumetric analysis).

concepts.name: Molarity (mol L^-1) and conversions
concepts.explanation: Concentration expressed as moles of solute per litre of solution, including calculations converting between molarity and grams per litre and determining moles from molarity and volume.

concepts.name: Calculations in titrations (formula method)
concepts.explanation: Use of molarity, volume, and stoichiometry (e.g., n = M × V and mole ratios from balanced equations) to solve quantitative volumetric analysis problems.

concepts.name: Volumetric analysis apparatus
concepts.explanation: Volumetric glassware and equipment commonly used in titrations: burette, pipette, volumetric flask, conical flask, and indicators; correct selection and use are essential for accurate results.

concepts.name: Correct titrimetric procedure
concepts.explanation: Step-by-step experimental technique for titration including rinsing and filling apparatus, accurate delivery of volumes, approaching the endpoint slowly, reading meniscus/burette, and recording titres to obtain concordant results.

concepts.name: HCl/NaOH titration and salt preparation (sodium chloride)
concepts.explanation: A practical titration experiment where hydrochloric acid is titrated with sodium hydroxide to determine concentration and demonstrate neutralisation; the reaction can be used to prepare sodium chloride.

concepts.name: Colour intensity as a function of concentration (qualitative treatment)
concepts.explanation: Observed relationship where the intensity of a solution's colour changes with concentration; used qualitatively to estimate concentration and introduce absorbance principles.

concepts.name: Neutralisation (formation of a salt)
concepts.explanation: Chemical reaction between an acid and a base producing a salt and usually water; concept includes stoichiometric relationships and practical examples.

concepts.name: Arrhenius theory of acids and bases (aqueous)
concepts.explanation: Definition of acids as substances that increase H+ concentration in aqueous solution and bases as substances that increase OH- concentration; applicable to aqueous titrations and neutralisation.

concepts.name: Combustion of hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Oxidation reactions of hydrocarbons producing CO2, H2O (and sometimes CO/soot) with large release of energy; key example reactions for alkanes and other fuels.

concepts.name: Heat of reaction and sign of ΔH
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change accompanying a chemical reaction; negative ΔH indicates exothermic (heat released), positive ΔH indicates endothermic (heat absorbed).

concepts.name: Heat of combustion and calorific value
concepts.explanation: Energy released when a specified amount (per mole or per kilogram) of a fuel is completely burned; used to compare fuels' energy content.

concepts.name: Bomb calorimeter
concepts.explanation: A laboratory instrument for accurately measuring heats of combustion by burning a sample in an oxygen-filled sealed vessel and measuring temperature rise.

concepts.name: Calorimetry experiment: neutralisation of HCl and NaOH
concepts.explanation: Mandatory laboratory procedure to determine the heat of reaction (neutralisation) by measuring temperature change upon mixing acid and alkali.

concepts.name: Fractional distillation of crude oil
concepts.explanation: Industrial separation of crude oil into fractions (refinery gas, gasoline, naphtha, kerosene, gas oil, residue) by different boiling-point ranges.

concepts.name: Composition of natural gas and LPG
concepts.explanation: Typical constituents of gaseous fuels: natural gas mainly methane (with ethane/propane traces); LPG mainly propane and/or butane.

concepts.name: Addition of mercaptans to natural gas
concepts.explanation: Use of strong-smelling sulfur compounds (mercaptans) as odorants to make otherwise odourless natural gas detectable for safety.

concepts.name: Octane number and engine knocking
concepts.explanation: Octane number quantifies a petrol's resistance to auto-ignition (knocking); higher octane means less tendency to knock under compression.

concepts.name: Methods to increase octane number (isomerisation, dehydrocyclisation, catalytic cracking)
concepts.explanation: Refinery chemical processes that convert straight-chain hydrocarbons into branched/cyclic/shorter molecules to improve petrol octane rating.

concepts.name: Alkanes, alkenes and alkynes as homologous series
concepts.explanation: Classification of saturated (alkanes), unsaturated single/double/triple-bonded hydrocarbons with general formulas and repeating CH2 patterns; for alkynes focus on ethyne.

concepts.name: Nomenclature and structural isomerism of alkanes to C5
concepts.explanation: Systematic naming (IUPAC style) and drawing of structural isomers for alkanes up to pentane (including recognition of branched structures).

concepts.name: Iso-octane (2,2,4-trimethylpentane) as a reference fuel
concepts.explanation: Structure and role of 2,2,4-trimethylpentane (iso-octane) used as the 100 reference point for the octane rating scale.

concepts.name: Physical properties of small hydrocarbons (state and solubility)
concepts.explanation: Properties such as physical state at STP and qualitative solubility (insoluble in water, soluble in non-polar solvents) illustrated by methane, ethene, ethyne and methylbenzene.

concepts.name: Tests for unsaturation (bromine water and acidified KMnO4)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative reactions where bromine water decolourises and acidified potassium manganate(VII) is reduced (decolourised/changed) by C=C or C≡C bonds to detect unsaturation.

concepts.name: Preparation and properties of ethyne (acetylene)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethyne, its combustion behavior, tests for unsaturation and its industrial use (e.g., oxyacetylene welding).

concepts.name: Hydrogen manufacture: electrolysis and steam reforming
concepts.explanation: Two principal hydrogen production methods: electrolysis of water (using electricity) and steam reforming of natural gas (industrial thermal/chemical process; simple treatment).

concepts.name: Aromatic hydrocarbons: benzene and alkylbenzenes
concepts.explanation: Structure and simple properties of benzene and its derivatives such as methylbenzene (toluene) and ethylbenzene as examples of aromatic compounds.

concepts.name: Oxyacetylene welding and cutting
concepts.explanation: Application of the high-temperature flame from acetylene/oxygen combustion for industrial welding and cutting of metals.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How changing temperature alters reaction rates—higher temperature increases kinetic energy, collision frequency and the fraction of collisions exceeding the activation energy, thus increasing rate.

concepts.name: Effect of concentration on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How reactant concentration affects the frequency of effective collisions and hence the rate of a chemical reaction; includes rate–concentration relationships used in kinetics experiments.

concepts.name: Catalysts and their effect on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Definition of catalysts and how they increase reaction rates by providing an alternate pathway with lower activation energy; distinction between homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis where appropriate.

concepts.name: Effect of particle size (surface area) on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How decreasing particle size (increasing surface area) of a solid reactant increases the area available for collisions and surface reactions, thereby increasing reaction rate for heterogeneous reactions.

concepts.name: Nature of reactants and its influence on rate
concepts.explanation: How the chemical identity of reactants (bond strengths, molecular complexity, ionic vs covalent character) affects the intrinsic speed of reactions and typical activation energies.

concepts.name: Catalyst poisons
concepts.explanation: Substances that reduce or eliminate catalyst activity by binding to active sites or otherwise deactivating the catalyst; implications for industrial and laboratory catalytic processes.

concepts.name: Enzymes as biological catalysts
concepts.explanation: Enzymes produced by living cells act as highly specific catalysts that accelerate biochemical reactions (examples include catalase and amylase), with concepts of specificity and active site.

concepts.name: Catalytic converters (function and environmental role)
concepts.explanation: Design and role of catalytic converters using metal catalysts (e.g., Pt, Pd, Rh) to convert CO, unburnt hydrocarbons and NOx into less harmful gases; reactions catalysed and environmental benefits.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment 6.1: Monitoring O2 production from H2O2 using MnO2
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure to measure the rate of oxygen evolution from hydrogen peroxide decomposition and investigate catalytic effects using manganese dioxide as a catalyst.

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment 6.2: Effects of concentration and temperature using sodium thiosulfate and HCl
concepts.explanation: Experimental study of how changing concentration and temperature affects reaction rate by timing the disappearance of a cross (sulfur precipitate) when sodium thiosulfate reacts with hydrochloric acid.

concepts.name: Demonstration: Oxidation of methanol using hot platinum or nichrome catalyst
concepts.explanation: Classroom demonstration of heterogeneous catalytic oxidation of methanol on a hot metal catalyst to illustrate catalytic action and reaction pathways on solid catalysts.

concepts.name: Demonstration: Oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by H2O2 catalysed by Co(II)
concepts.explanation: Demonstration of homogeneous catalysis where cobalt(II) salts accelerate the oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by hydrogen peroxide, showing rate enhancement in solution.

concepts.name: Dust explosions as a kinetics hazard
concepts.explanation: The phenomenon where fine combustible dust suspended in air can undergo very rapid oxidation/explosion due to high surface area and rapid propagation of reaction—illustrates practical importance of particle size and concentration.
concepts.broader_concept: Applications and safety relating to reaction rates

concepts.name: Rate of reaction (definition and units)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative definition of reaction rate as change in concentration (or amount, mass, pressure) of a reactant or product per unit time, including common units (mol L^-1 s^-1, g s^-1, Pa s^-1) and sign conventions.

concepts.name: Average and instantaneous rate
concepts.explanation: Difference between average rate over a time interval and instantaneous rate at a specific time (slope of concentration vs time curve), including how to estimate graphically.

concepts.name: Rate law and rate constant (k)
concepts.explanation: Expression relating reaction rate to reactant concentrations raised to powers (rate = k[A]^m[B]^n...), interpretation of rate constant k and its dependence on temperature.

concepts.name: Order of reaction (overall and partial)
concepts.explanation: Definition of reaction order with respect to a single reactant (partial order) and overall order as the sum of exponents in the rate law; distinction from stoichiometric coefficients.

concepts.name: Methods for determining reaction order (initial rates and graphical methods)
concepts.explanation: Experimental approaches to find reaction orders: initial rates method (varying initial concentrations), and graphical tests using concentration-time, ln(conc)-time, and 1/conc-time plots.

concepts.name: Integrated rate laws (zero, first, second order)
concepts.explanation: Mathematical integrated forms linking concentration and time for zero-, first-, and second-order reactions, used to model concentration vs time and to extract k.

concepts.name: Half-life of reactions (first-order)
concepts.explanation: Definition and calculation of half-life (t1/2), with emphasis on the constant half-life property of first-order reactions: t1/2 = ln(2)/k.

concepts.name: Collision theory
concepts.explanation: Model explaining that reaction rate depends on frequency of effective collisions between reactant particles and the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy and proper orientation.

concepts.name: Activation energy and the transition state
concepts.explanation: Concept of activation energy (Ea) as the minimum energy barrier for reaction, and the transition state as a high-energy activated complex along the reaction coordinate.

concepts.name: Arrhenius equation and temperature dependence of k
concepts.explanation: Relationship k = A e^{-Ea/RT} linking rate constant to activation energy and temperature, including how to use ln k vs 1/T (Arrhenius plot) to determine Ea and A.

concepts.name: Reaction mechanism and rate-determining step
concepts.explanation: Concept of a sequence of elementary steps making up an overall reaction, and the slowest elementary step controlling the observed rate; linking mechanism to the rate law.

concepts.name: Effect of surface area and particle size
concepts.explanation: How increasing surface area (smaller particle size) for heterogeneous reactions increases frequency of collisions at reactive interfaces and thus accelerates rate.

concepts.name: Catalysts and inhibitors (homogeneous and heterogeneous)
concepts.explanation: Role of catalysts in providing alternative lower-energy pathways (and inhibitors in reducing rate), distinction between homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysis and examples (enzymes, solid catalysts).

concepts.name: Experimental methods to measure reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Practical techniques for following reaction progress: gas collection (volume/time), mass loss, colorimetry/spectrophotometry, conductivity, titration of aliquots, and pressure measurements.

concepts.name: Iodine clock reaction (demonstration experiment)
concepts.explanation: Classic school experiment where time to sudden appearance of color indicates rate; used to investigate effects of concentration, temperature, and catalysts on rate.

concepts.name: Marble chips and dilute acid (gas evolution experiment)
concepts.explanation: Practical procedure measuring rate of reaction by collecting CO2 gas from CaCO3 + HCl (or by mass loss), used to study effects of concentration, surface area, and temperature.

concepts.name: Tetrahedral carbon (sp3 geometry)
concepts.explanation: Carbon atom bonded to four single bonds in a tetrahedral arrangement (sp3 hybridisation); basis for saturated compounds such as alkanes; use of models to show three-dimensional shape.

concepts.name: Alkanes (saturated hydrocarbons)
concepts.explanation: Hydrocarbons containing only single C–C and C–H bonds (saturated); simple nomenclature up to four carbons, physical state and qualitative solubility, and use as fuels.

concepts.name: Alcohols: structure, nomenclature and classification
concepts.explanation: Organic compounds containing an —OH group; naming and structures up to four carbons; distinction between primary and secondary alcohols.

concepts.name: Oxidation of alcohols (KMnO4 / Na2Cr2O7)
concepts.explanation: Oxidation reactions converting alcohols to aldehydes and further to carboxylic acids using oxidants such as KMnO4 or Na2Cr2O7 (half-equations at introductory level).

concepts.name: Solubility comparison of short-chain alcohols
concepts.explanation: Experimentally comparing solubility of methanol and butan-1-ol in (i) cyclohexane and (ii) water to illustrate polarity and hydrogen-bonding effects.

concepts.name: Ethanol: fermentation production and uses
concepts.explanation: Biochemical fermentation as an industrial and laboratory method for producing ethanol; uses of ethanol as a fuel and as an industrial/household solvent; role in brewing and distilling.

concepts.name: Methanol: properties and use as a denaturant
concepts.explanation: Simple alcohol (methanol) properties and its use to denature ethanol-containing products (rendering them unfit for consumption).
concepts.broader_concept: Uses and hazards of simple alcohols

concepts.name: Planar carbon (sp2 geometry) and double bonds
concepts.explanation: Carbon atoms with trigonal planar geometry (sp2 hybridisation) as found in alkenes and carbonyls; the non-polar C=C double bond and polar C=O double bond contrasted.

concepts.name: Alkenes and addition reactions
concepts.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing C=C bonds; undergo electrophilic addition reactions with hydrogen (hydrogenation), halogens, water (hydration), and hydrogen halides; write balanced structural equations.

concepts.name: Polymerisation of ethene and propene
concepts.explanation: Addition polymerisation of simple alkenes (ethene and propene) to form polymers (conceptual level; mechanism not required).

concepts.name: Carbonyl compounds (aldehydes) — structure and reactivity
concepts.explanation: Aldehydes containing a polar C=O group; nomenclature and structure up to four carbons; reactivity including oxidation to carboxylic acids.

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids: structure, properties and examples
concepts.explanation: Organic acids with the —COOH group; nomenclature up to four carbons; physical properties including solubility trends; examples such as methanoic acid (nettles/ants) and ethanoic acid (vinegar).

concepts.name: Benzene and aromaticity (circle representation)
concepts.explanation: Benzene ring represented with a circle to indicate delocalised bonding (intermediate between single and double bonds); planar aromatic structure and relative unreactivity toward addition reactions.

concepts.name: Aromatic compounds: applications and hazards
concepts.explanation: Aromatic compounds form the basis of dyes, detergents, herbicides and many pharmaceuticals; some (e.g., benzene) are carcinogenic while others (e.g., aspirin) are not—societal relevance and safety considerations.
concepts.broader_concept: Applications and safety of aromatic compounds

concepts.name: Aromatic acid-base indicators
concepts.explanation: Use of aromatic-derived indicators (examples: phenolphthalein, methyl orange) to signal pH changes; structures not required at this level.

concepts.name: Substitution reactions: halogenation of alkanes
concepts.explanation: Free-radical substitution of hydrogen atoms in alkanes by halogens (conceptual level; write balanced structural equations where required).

concepts.name: Elimination reactions: dehydration of alcohols
concepts.explanation: Removal of elements (e.g., water) from alcohols to form alkenes (dehydration) as an example of an elimination reaction.

concepts.name: Combustion and flammability of organic compounds
concepts.explanation: Combustion as a common reaction of organic compounds (including alcohols); note that fully halogenated alkanes are non-flammable.

concepts.name: PVC synthesis from ethene
concepts.explanation: Industrial organic synthesis route converting ethene to polyvinyl chloride (PVC), including key reaction steps, monomer formation and polymerisation.

concepts.name: Principles of organic synthesis: bond breaking and bond forming
concepts.explanation: Fundamental concepts in designing organic syntheses: identifying bonds to be broken and bonds to be formed during transformations.

concepts.name: Reactions of carboxylic acids with metals, bases and carbonates
concepts.explanation: Characteristic acid reactions: metal-acid reaction (e.g., with Mg) producing hydrogen, neutralisation with NaOH, and reaction with Na2CO3 producing CO2.

concepts.name: Reaction of alcohols with sodium
concepts.explanation: Acid–base reaction where alcohols react with sodium metal to form alkoxides and hydrogen gas (R–OH + Na → R–O−Na+ + 1/2 H2).

concepts.name: Saponification (soap manufacture)
concepts.explanation: Hydrolysis of triglycerides with strong base (NaOH) to yield glycerol and soap (carboxylate salts); industrial soap-making principles.

concepts.name: Solvent extraction (liquid–liquid extraction)
concepts.explanation: Separation technique using differential solubility of compounds between immiscible liquids to isolate organic natural products.

concepts.name: Steam distillation for natural product extraction
concepts.explanation: Technique to isolate volatile organic compounds (e.g., essential oils) from plant material by co-distillation with water at temperatures below decomposition.

concepts.name: Chromatography as a separation and analysis method
concepts.explanation: Principles and basic methods of chromatography (e.g., TLC, column) for separating and analysing organic mixtures and natural products.

concepts.name: Oxidation of ethanol to ethanal in human metabolism
concepts.explanation: Biochemical oxidation of ethanol to ethanal (acetaldehyde) by alcohol dehydrogenase as the first metabolic step in humans.

concepts.name: Alcohols as motor fuels
concepts.explanation: Use of alcohols (e.g., ethanol, methanol) as motor fuels: combustion properties, energy content, advantages and limitations.

concepts.name: Scope of the petrochemical industry (examples of synthetic products)
concepts.explanation: Overview of petrochemical industry outputs with representative examples of synthetic products (e.g., polymers, solvents), and their feedstocks.

concepts.name: Examples of useful products from organic synthesis (aspirin, paracetamol)
concepts.explanation: Representative pharmaceutical products produced by organic synthesis, illustrating application of synthetic methods to make useful molecules.

concepts.name: Flame retardant materials: function and examples
concepts.explanation: Chemical principles of flame retardants, how they inhibit combustion (e.g., chemical quenching, char formation) and common examples used in materials.

concepts.name: Chemical agents used in fire extinguishers
concepts.explanation: Common chemical extinguishing agents (e.g., CO2, foam, dry powder), their chemical action (smothering, cooling, interrupting combustion) and typical uses.

concepts.name: Chromatography (principles: mobile and stationary phases, selective adsorption)
concepts.explanation: Fundamental principles of chromatographic separation: a mobile phase carrying a mixture moves in contact with a selectively adsorbent stationary phase, causing components to separate based on differential adsorption/partitioning.

concepts.name: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) — laboratory procedure and application
concepts.explanation: Practical TLC technique: preparing and spotting plates, developing in a solvent, visualising spots, calculating Rf values; applied use in separating dyes from fibres (forensic analysis).

concepts.name: Gas chromatography (GC) — basic principles
concepts.explanation: Instrumental chromatographic method where a gaseous mobile phase carries volatile analytes through a column with a stationary phase; separation depends on volatility and interactions with the stationary phase and is detected by an appropriate detector.

concepts.name: High-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) — basic principles
concepts.explanation: High-resolution chromatographic technique using a liquid mobile phase under pressure and a packed stationary phase to separate components; includes concept of different stationary phases and detectors (overview level).

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry (basic principles)
concepts.explanation: Overview of mass spectrometry as an instrumental analytical method: ionisation of molecules, separation of ions by mass-to-charge ratio and detection (principles only; detailed spectral interpretation not required at this level).

concepts.name: Recrystallisation (purification of benzoic acid)
concepts.explanation: Purification technique for solid organic compounds that relies on differential solubility in hot vs cold solvent to remove impurities, demonstrated by recrystallising benzoic acid.

concepts.name: Melting point determination as a purity test
concepts.explanation: Measuring the melting point and melting range of a solid to assess identity and purity; pure crystalline compounds have sharp melting points while impurities broaden and depress the range.

concepts.name: Chromatographic separation of indicator mixtures (paper, TLC, column)
concepts.explanation: Separation and identification of components in a mixture using paper chromatography, thin-layer chromatography, or column chromatography based on differential partitioning or adsorption.

concepts.name: Steam distillation for extraction of essential oils (clove oil)
concepts.explanation: Isolation of volatile, water-immiscible organic compounds from plant material by co-distillation with steam to allow distillation below their normal boiling points.

concepts.name: Tests for unsaturation (alkenes): acidified potassium manganate(VII) and bromine water
concepts.explanation: Qualitative tests for carbon–carbon double bonds: oxidative decolourisation of acidified KMnO4 (or permanganate) and addition/decolourisation of bromine water indicating unsaturation.

concepts.name: Preparation of ethene (alkene formation by elimination) and its combustion
concepts.explanation: Laboratory generation of ethene (typical dehydration/elimination methods) and study of its combustion behaviour as a representative alkene.

concepts.name: Preparation and qualitative tests of ethanal (aldehyde reactions)
concepts.explanation: Synthesis of ethanal (partial oxidation of ethanol or other lab methods) and its characteristic reactions: oxidation by KMnO4, reduction tests with Fehling's reagent, and ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens') producing a silver mirror.

concepts.name: Preparation and reactions of ethanoic acid (acid–carbonate and acid–metal reactions)
concepts.explanation: Synthesis/characterisation of ethanoic acid and demonstration of typical carboxylic acid reactions: reaction with sodium carbonate producing CO2 and reaction with magnesium producing hydrogen and a salt.

concepts.name: Preparation of soap (saponification of fats/oils)
concepts.explanation: Formation of soap by alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) of esters (triglycerides) to produce glycerol and the sodium salts of fatty acids (soap), including isolation and properties.

concepts.name: Dynamic equilibrium and reversible reactions
concepts.explanation: Definition of reversible reactions and dynamic chemical equilibrium: at equilibrium the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal and macroscopic concentrations remain constant.

concepts.name: Equilibrium law and constant (Kc)
concepts.explanation: Law of mass action: expression of the equilibrium constant Kc for homogeneous reactions in terms of reactant and product concentrations; Kc depends on temperature and quantifies equilibrium composition.

concepts.name: Le Chatelier's Principle
concepts.explanation: Predictive principle stating that a system at equilibrium responds to external stresses (changes in concentration, pressure, temperature) by shifting to oppose the change.

concepts.name: Effect of concentration changes on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: How adding or removing reactants or products shifts the equilibrium position (toward products when reactants added, etc.), including common-ion shifts in solution equilibria.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature changes on equilibrium position
concepts.explanation: How heating or cooling shifts equilibria depending on whether the reaction is exothermic or endothermic, and the associated temperature dependence of Kc.

concepts.name: Effect of pressure (and volume) changes on gas-phase equilibria
concepts.explanation: How changes in pressure or volume affect equilibria involving gases: equilibrium shifts toward the side with fewer moles of gas when pressure is increased (and vice versa).

concepts.name: Effect of a catalyst on equilibrium
concepts.explanation: Role of catalysts in equilibria: catalysts increase the rates of forward and reverse reactions equally and therefore do not change the equilibrium position, only the speed at which equilibrium is reached.

concepts.name: Cobalt(II) chloride / hexaaquacobalt(II) equilibrium experiment
concepts.explanation: Demonstration using CoCl4^2- ↔ [Co(H2O)6]^2+ (colour change blue ↔ pink) to illustrate effects of temperature and concentration on an equilibrium mixture.
concepts.broader_concept: Laboratory demonstrations of Le Chatelier's principle

concepts.name: Dichromate ↔ chromate equilibrium with hydrogen peroxide experiment
concepts.explanation: Use of the Cr2O7^2- / CrO4^2- equilibrium (and reaction with H2O2 and H+) to demonstrate shifts in equilibrium and colour changes on changing concentration/conditions.
concepts.broader_concept: Laboratory demonstrations of Le Chatelier's principle

concepts.name: Iron(III) thiocyanate equilibrium experiment
concepts.explanation: Demonstration of Fe3+ + SCN- ⇌ Fe(SCN)2+ (red complex) used to show how changing concentrations shifts equilibrium and affects observable colour/intensity.
concepts.broader_concept: Laboratory demonstrations of Le Chatelier's principle

concepts.name: Haber process — industrial application of Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.explanation: Industrial synthesis of ammonia from N2 and H2: uses high pressures, moderate temperatures and catalysts to shift equilibrium toward ammonia and optimize yield and rate.

concepts.name: Catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide (Contact Process step)
concepts.explanation: Industrial oxidation of SO2 to SO3 using a vanadium(V) oxide catalyst; demonstrates application of Le Chatelier's principles (temperature, pressure, catalyst) to maximize SO3 yield.

concepts.name: pH scale and calculation for strong acids/bases
concepts.explanation: Definition of the pH scale; calculating pH for dilute aqueous solutions of strong acids and strong bases (limitations: dilute aqueous solutions only; mixtures not required).

concepts.name: Universal indicator: use and limitations
concepts.explanation: Use of universal indicator paper or solution to estimate pH and discussion of its limitations (accuracy and confinement to dilute aqueous solutions).

concepts.name: pH meter: principle and practical pH determination
concepts.explanation: Principle of pH meters and their use for determining solution pH as an instrumental method of analysis.

concepts.name: Hardness in water: causes of temporary and permanent hardness
concepts.explanation: Distinction between temporary hardness (typically bicarbonate salts) and permanent hardness (typically sulfate/chloride salts); causes and implications for water use.
concepts.broader_concept: Water hardness and its chemical causes

concepts.name: Removal of temporary hardness by boiling
concepts.explanation: Practical and theoretical explanation of how boiling removes temporary hardness by precipitating carbonate scale (e.g., CaCO3 formation).

concepts.name: Ion exchange and deionisation for removal of hardness
concepts.explanation: Principles of ion-exchange resins and deionisation processes used to remove hardness-causing cations (e.g., Ca2+, Mg2+) from water.

concepts.name: Test for scale deposits in kettles (carbonate scale identification)
concepts.explanation: Simple tests and observations to identify limescale/scale deposits (carbonate-based) formed in kettles and hot-water systems.

concepts.name: Physical water-treatment processes: sedimentation, flocculation and filtration
concepts.explanation: Mechanisms and purposes of sedimentation, flocculation and filtration as primary physical steps in water treatment to remove suspended solids.

concepts.name: Chlorination and colorimetric estimation of free chlorine
concepts.explanation: Use of chlorine for disinfection of water; colorimetric methods (or comparators) to estimate free chlorine concentration (linked to mandatory experiment 9.1).

concepts.name: Fluoridation and pH adjustment in water treatment
concepts.explanation: Addition of fluoride for dental health where applied and chemical adjustment of pH in water treatment to meet safety/quality requirements.

concepts.name: Sewage treatment stages: primary, secondary and tertiary
concepts.explanation: Overview of sewage treatment: primary (screening/settlement), secondary (biological/bacterial breakdown) and tertiary (removal/reduction of nutrients like phosphates and nitrates), including cost considerations for tertiary treatment.

concepts.name: Eutrophication: role of nitrates and phosphates
concepts.explanation: How nutrient inputs (nitrates, phosphates) drive algal blooms and eutrophication, with ecological consequences for water bodies.

concepts.name: Colorimetry: principle and applications in water analysis
concepts.explanation: Principle of colorimetric analysis (absorbance-concentration relationship) and its application to measuring species in water (e.g., chlorine, nutrients, some metal assays).

concepts.name: Determination of total suspended solids (TSS) and total dissolved solids (TDS)
concepts.explanation: Practical method for measuring TSS and TDS by filtration and evaporation respectively and reporting as ppm (mandatory experiment 9.2).
concepts.broader_concept: Quantification of particulate and dissolved matter in water

concepts.name: Qualitative tests for common anions in water
concepts.explanation: Specific qualitative chemical tests for common anions found in water (e.g., chloride, sulfate, nitrate) as part of ionic analysis.

concepts.name: Regulatory limits for contaminants in water (EU examples)
concepts.explanation: Awareness of statutory/health-based limits for chemical species in drinking/river water with examples (e.g., nitrates, phosphates, specific metal ions).

concepts.name: Analysis of lead in water: significance and basic detection approaches
concepts.explanation: Importance of monitoring lead in water and common approaches to its determination (brief reference to instrumental/chemical detection).

concepts.name: Organic chemical pollutants in water: sources and examples
concepts.explanation: Identification of common organic pollutants (sewage, industrial waste, silage effluent, milk) and their relevance to water quality analysis and treatment.

concepts.name: Batch industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: A mode of production where reactants are charged into a reactor for a set time, the reaction proceeds, products are removed, and the cycle is repeated — common for small-scale, flexible manufacture and multi-product plants.

concepts.name: Continuous industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: A production method in which reactants are fed and products removed continuously, enabling steady-state operation, high throughput and efficient use of equipment for large-scale manufacture.

concepts.name: Semi-continuous (semi-batch) industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: A hybrid process where one or more reactants are added or removed during a reaction while other components remain in a reactor; used to control reaction rates, heat, or selectivity.

concepts.name: Feedstock (raw material) selection in industrial processes
concepts.explanation: The choice and quality of raw materials used in an industrial chemical process, including availability, purity, cost, and suitability, which strongly affect yield, economics and environmental impact.
concepts.broader_concept: Characteristics of effective industrial chemical processes

concepts.name: Characteristics of effective industrial chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Key criteria used to evaluate industrial processes, such as feedstock suitability, yield and selectivity, scalability, safety, cost-effectiveness and environmental performance.

concepts.name: Effect of temperature and pressure on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How changes in temperature and pressure influence the speed of chemical reactions (collision frequency, activation energy effects, pressure effects on gaseous reactants).

concepts.name: Catalyst effect on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: The role of catalysts in increasing reaction rates by providing alternative pathways with lower activation energy and their practical use in industrial processes.

concepts.name: Factors affecting product yield (temperature, pressure, catalysts)
concepts.explanation: How temperature, pressure and catalysts affect equilibrium positions and conversion, and thus the yield of desired products in chemical reactions.

concepts.name: Cost reduction strategies in chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Techniques used to lower production costs, including heat integration (heat exchangers), use of catalysts, recycling of materials, and valorization/sale of co-products.

concepts.name: Separation and recovery of co-products
concepts.explanation: Methods for separating, purifying, and recovering useful co-products from reaction mixtures for disposal or sale (e.g., distillation, extraction, crystallization).

concepts.name: Wastewater treatment processes in chemical industry
concepts.explanation: Principles and techniques for treating industrial effluents, including primary, secondary and tertiary treatments to remove contaminants before discharge.

concepts.name: Air emission control methods in chemical plants
concepts.explanation: Technologies and practices to control gaseous emissions from chemical processes (scrubbers, filters, catalytic converters, monitoring).

concepts.name: Quality control procedures in chemical manufacturing
concepts.explanation: Analytical testing, standards, and in-process checks used to ensure product specification, purity and consistency during production.

concepts.name: Process safety and hazard monitoring
concepts.explanation: Identification, monitoring and mitigation of process hazards including training, instrumentation, safety features and emergency procedures in chemical operations.

concepts.name: Site selection for chemical manufacturing plants
concepts.explanation: Considerations for locating chemical facilities, including access to raw materials, utilities, transport, environmental impact, and community safety.

concepts.name: Fixed and variable costs in chemical production
concepts.explanation: Distinction between fixed (capital, plant) and variable (raw materials, energy) costs and their roles in process economics and decision making.

concepts.name: Corrosion resistance and prevention
concepts.explanation: Mechanisms of corrosion (electrochemical oxidation), factors affecting corrosion, and methods to prevent or slow corrosion (passivation, coatings, cathodic protection, material selection).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Materials for chemical plant construction (unreactive, corrosion-resistant materials)
concepts.explanation: Selection criteria and properties of materials used to construct chemical plant equipment — chemical inertness, corrosion resistance, mechanical strength and examples (stainless steels, glass-lined vessels, polymers, ceramics).

concepts.name: Water purification methods (chemical treatment)
concepts.explanation: Chemical processes used to produce pure water, including coagulation/flocculation, chlorination/disinfection, ion exchange, adsorption (activated carbon) and chemical dosing for contaminant removal.

concepts.name: Surfactants and detergents: structure–function relationships
concepts.explanation: Amphiphilic molecular structure of surfactants, micelle formation, critical micelle concentration, and how these properties enable emulsification and cleaning action in detergents.

concepts.name: Semiconductors: chemical basis and materials
concepts.explanation: Chemical and electronic principles underlying semiconducting materials — band gaps, doping, common semiconductor materials (Si, GaAs), and how composition and structure control electronic properties.

concepts.name: Liquid crystals: molecular structure and phase behavior
concepts.explanation: Relationship between molecular shape/chemistry and mesophase formation (nematic, smectic), orientational order, and application of liquid crystalline materials in displays.

concepts.name: Dyes and pigments: chromophores and color chemistry
concepts.explanation: Chemical origins of color in dyes and pigments (conjugated systems, chromophores, auxochromes), principles of light absorption, and considerations for dye/pigment selection and application in paints and textiles.

concepts.name: Extraction and properties of metals
concepts.explanation: Chemical methods for obtaining metals (pyrometallurgy, hydrometallurgy, electrolysis), key properties of metals relevant to use in industry, and implications for supply and applications.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Enzyme catalysis (industrial and chemical principles)
concepts.explanation: Basic chemical principles of enzyme catalysis: active sites, specificity, reaction mechanisms, and applications of enzymes in industrial processes and detergents.

concepts.name: Haber process (ammonia synthesis)
concepts.explanation: Industrial synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen; overall equation N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3 and key conditions (high pressure, iron catalyst, elevated temperature)

concepts.name: Urea synthesis from ammonia and carbon dioxide
concepts.explanation: Conversion of ammonia and carbon dioxide to urea (industrial route used in fertiliser production); overall stoichiometric equation 2NH3 + CO2 -> NH2CONH2 + H2O
concepts.broader_concept: Conversion of ammonia to fertiliser products

concepts.name: Ostwald process (nitric acid manufacture from ammonia)
concepts.explanation: Industrial production of nitric acid from ammonia by catalytic oxidation to NO, followed by further oxidation and absorption to give HNO3; key overall first-step equation 4NH3 + 5O2 -> 4NO + 6H2O (catalytic)

concepts.name: Oxidation of nitrogen monoxide
concepts.explanation: Gas-phase oxidation of nitric oxide to nitrogen dioxide required in nitric acid manufacture: 2NO + O2 -> 2NO2
concepts.broader_concept: Oxidation steps in nitric acid manufacture

concepts.name: Ammonium nitrate formation (acid-base reaction)
concepts.explanation: Formation of ammonium nitrate fertilizer by neutralising nitric acid with ammonia: HNO3 + NH3 -> NH4NO3
concepts.broader_concept: Fertiliser manufacture from nitric acid and ammonia

concepts.name: Magnesium oxide manufacture from seawater (precipitation and calcination)
concepts.explanation: Extraction of Mg2+ from seawater by precipitation as Mg(OH)2 (Mg2+ + 2OH- -> Mg(OH)2(s)) followed by calcination to MgO (Mg(OH)2 -> MgO + H2O)

concepts.name: Magnesium oxide as a refractory material
concepts.explanation: Use of MgO (magnesia) for high-temperature, heat-resistant linings (refractory) in furnace walls due to high melting point and chemical stability
concepts.broader_concept: Properties and applications of inorganic oxides

concepts.name: Structured chemical plant visit (educational procedure)
concepts.explanation: Planned, guided visit to an industrial chemical plant with defined learning objectives, pre-visit preparation and post-visit analysis to study real-world chemical processes safely

concepts.name: Case study of an industrial chemical process
concepts.explanation: Classroom-based study method examining one industrial chemical process in depth (e.g., ammonia to urea, nitric acid production, or MgO manufacture) applying relevant chemical principles and equations

concepts.name: Synthetic polymers (plastics and synthetic fibres) as industrial products
concepts.explanation: Recognition of plastics and synthetic fibres as major products of the chemical industry, their role as engineered materials and typical industrial applications

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect and role of CO2 and H2O
concepts.explanation: How greenhouse gases (notably CO2 and water vapour) trap outgoing infrared radiation, and how increased atmospheric CO2 from human activity enhances warming

concepts.name: Combustion of carbon to give CO and CO2
concepts.explanation: Chemical reactions of carbon combustion under different oxygen supplies producing carbon monoxide (incomplete combustion) or carbon dioxide (complete combustion)

concepts.name: Carbon monoxide: neutral oxide and toxic gas
concepts.explanation: Classification of CO as a neutral oxide (no acidic/basic behavior) and its toxic properties due to binding to haemoglobin

concepts.name: Carbon dioxide as an acidic oxide and dissolution in water
concepts.explanation: CO2 reacts with water to form carbonic acid, explaining acidic behavior of dissolved CO2 and ocean uptake reducing atmospheric CO2

concepts.name: Fermentation as a source of CO2
concepts.explanation: Biochemical fermentation of sugars to ethanol produces carbon dioxide as a byproduct (e.g., in brewing/baking)

concepts.name: Diatomic nitrogen structure and inertness (N≡N)
concepts.explanation: The triple bond in N2 gives high bond energy and low reactivity, explaining the general inertness of molecular nitrogen
concepts.broader_concept: Bonding and Reactivity of Diatomic Molecules

concepts.name: Natural nitrogen fixation and the nitrogen cycle
concepts.explanation: Processes (biological, lightning, soil chemistry) that convert N2 into reactive nitrogen compounds and the cyclical movement of nitrogen through ecosystems

concepts.name: Formation of NOx by electric discharge (lightning)
concepts.explanation: High-energy electric discharges cause N2 and O2 to react forming nitrogen oxides (NO, NO2) important in atmospheric chemistry
concepts.broader_concept: Atmospheric Formation of Reactive Nitrogen Species

concepts.name: Industrial manufacture of oxygen by liquefaction and fractional distillation of air
concepts.explanation: Cooling air to liquefy it and separating component gases by boiling point differences in fractional distillation to produce O2 (and N2, Ar)

concepts.name: Sources of NOx and SO2 (natural, domestic, industrial, combustion engines)
concepts.explanation: Identification of major sources that emit nitrogen oxides and sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere, including fossil fuel combustion and natural processes

concepts.name: Dissolution of NO2 and SO2 forming acids (acid rain precursors)
concepts.explanation: NO2 and SO2 dissolve in water to form nitric and sulfurous/sulfuric acids, leading to acidified precipitation

concepts.name: Flue-gas desulfurization using limestone (scrubbing)
concepts.explanation: Chemical removal of SO2 from waste gases by reaction with limestone (CaCO3/CaO) to form calcium sulfite/sulfate as a pollution-control method

concepts.name: Formation of ozone in the stratosphere (O2 photodissociation → O3)
concepts.explanation: Ultraviolet photodissociation of O2 produces atomic oxygen which combines with O2 to form ozone (O3), creating the stratospheric ozone layer

concepts.name: Chloroalkane preparation by chlorination of alkanes (radical halogenation)
concepts.explanation: Free-radical substitution of hydrogen by chlorine on alkanes (e.g., methane → chloromethane) as a route to produce chloroalkanes

concepts.name: CFCs and ozone depletion (chlorine-catalysed ozone destruction)
concepts.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine radicals in the stratosphere that catalyse ozone breakdown, reducing ozone concentration
concepts.broader_concept: Anthropogenic Impacts on the Ozone Layer

concepts.name: Types of crystal lattices: ionic, molecular, metallic, covalent macromolecular and related properties
concepts.explanation: Classification of solids by bonding type and lattice (ionic, molecular, metallic, giant covalent) and how bonding explains melting point, conductivity, hardness

concepts.name: X-ray scattering (X-ray crystallography) for determining crystal structure (Braggs)
concepts.explanation: Use of X-ray diffraction/scattering to probe and determine atomic arrangements in crystals (historical contribution: Bragg's development of the technique)

concepts.name: Addition polymerisation of alkenes (production of polyethene, PVC, polystyrene)
concepts.explanation: Mechanism and practice of addition polymerisation of alkene monomers to form common polymers and how monomer structure affects polymer properties

concepts.name: Recycling of polystyrene: sorting, shredding, washing, drying and re-extrusion
concepts.explanation: Practical stages in mechanical recycling of polystyrene plastic including preparation and reprocessing steps

concepts.name: Electrical conductivity of metals
concepts.explanation: Ability of metals to conduct electric current due to mobile electrons in the metallic lattice; contrasts with non-metals which are typically poor conductors.

concepts.name: Thermal conductivity of metals
concepts.explanation: Capacity of metals to transfer heat efficiently via free electrons and lattice vibrations, generally higher than in non-metals.

concepts.name: Malleability
concepts.explanation: Mechanical property describing a metal's ability to be deformed plastically (hammered or rolled) into thin sheets without breaking.

concepts.name: Ductility
concepts.explanation: Mechanical property referring to a metal's ability to be drawn into wires without fracture, related to plastic deformation mechanisms.

concepts.name: Hardness of metals
concepts.explanation: Resistance of a metal to localized plastic deformation or scratching; measurable by standard tests and influenced by composition and microstructure.

concepts.name: Metallic lustre
concepts.explanation: Characteristic shiny appearance of metals caused by reflection of light from delocalized electrons at the surface.
concepts.broader_concept: Optical and surface properties of metals

concepts.name: Alloys and their properties
concepts.explanation: Materials composed of two or more elements (one typically a metal) whose combined composition alters mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties compared with pure metals.

concepts.name: Effect of carbon content on steel hardness
concepts.explanation: How varying carbon concentration in iron-carbon alloys (steel) increases hardness and strength through formation of different microstructures (e.g., pearlite, martensite).

concepts.name: Experimental comparison of metals and non-metals (tests for conductivity, malleability, hardness, lustre)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedures to compare sample materials using simple tests: electrical circuit or multimeter for conductivity, bending/hammering for malleability, scratch or indentation tests for hardness, and visual inspection for lustre.
concepts.broader_concept: Practical methods for determining material properties

concepts.name: Electrochemical series
concepts.explanation: An ordered list of metals (and ions) by standard electrode potential used to predict direction of redox reactions, relative cell voltages and relative corrodibility.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Simple electrochemical (galvanic) cells — metal combinations and cell voltage
concepts.explanation: How different combinations of two metals (electrodes) in a simple cell produce different voltages; using electrode potentials to calculate cell EMF.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of molten salts (experimental: molten lead bromide)
concepts.explanation: Electrolytic decomposition of molten ionic compounds (e.g., PbBr2) using inert electrodes: identification of half‑reactions, products (metal deposition, halogen evolution) and cell operation.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Inert electrodes in electrolysis
concepts.explanation: Use and role of inert electrodes (e.g., graphite, platinum) that conduct electrons but do not chemically react with electrolysis products.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion of metals — mechanisms and relative corrodibility
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical oxidation of metals (rusting and other corrosion processes), factors affecting rate and comparison of susceptibility between metals.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion prevention — galvanising and surface coating
concepts.explanation: Methods to prevent corrosion: protective barrier coatings and sacrificial protection such as galvanising (zinc coating) and how they protect underlying metal.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolytic extraction of aluminium (Hall–Héroult principles)
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical extraction of aluminium from alumina dissolved in molten cryolite: cathodic reduction to aluminium, anodic reactions, high energy demand and process considerations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolytic extraction of sodium (molten salt electrolysis)
concepts.explanation: Production of sodium metal by electrolysis of molten sodium chloride: cell requirements, product separation and design considerations to prevent recombination.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Recycling of aluminium
concepts.explanation: Processes and importance of recycling aluminium, energy savings compared with primary electrolytic production and material recovery considerations.

concepts.name: Transition elements — general chemical properties (colour, catalytic behaviour)
concepts.explanation: Common properties of d‑block metals: formation of coloured ions, multiple oxidation states, and roles as catalysts in chemical reactions.

concepts.name: Manufacture of iron — blast furnace chemical aspects
concepts.explanation: Chemical reactions in the blast furnace for iron production: reduction of iron oxides by carbon monoxide/coke, formation of slag and main reaction stages.

concepts.name: Steels as alloys of iron — composition and properties
concepts.explanation: Concept of steel as iron alloyed with controlled carbon and other elements; how composition influences mechanical properties and uses.

concepts.name: Electric arc process for steel manufacture (overview)
concepts.explanation: Outline of the electric arc furnace method for steelmaking: melting scrap or direct reduced iron using electric arcs and main operational stages.

concepts.name: Environmental aspects of iron and steel production
concepts.explanation: Environmental impacts of iron and steel manufacture including greenhouse gas emissions, particulates and resource consumption, and mitigation measures.

concepts.name: Uses of iron and steel (applications)
concepts.explanation: Common applications of iron and steel in construction, transportation and manufacturing and how material properties determine use.

concepts.name: Periodic table: arrangement and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: The periodic table as an ordered arrangement of elements that reveals repeating (periodic) trends in physical and chemical properties across periods and down groups.

concepts.name: Subatomic particles: electrons, protons and neutrons
concepts.explanation: Properties of electrons, protons and neutrons including relative mass, relative charge and their locations within the atom.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometer: role and fundamental processes
concepts.explanation: Use of the mass spectrometer to determine relative atomic masses and its fundamental processes: vaporisation, production of positive ions, acceleration, separation and detection (qualitative).

concepts.name: Electronic structure and energy levels for elements 1–20
concepts.explanation: Organisation of electrons into main energy levels for the first 20 elements and classification of these elements based on number of outer (valence) electrons.

concepts.name: Emission and absorption spectra; Balmer series
concepts.explanation: Emission and absorption spectra concepts with the Balmer series of hydrogen as an example; line spectra used as evidence for discrete atomic energy levels.

concepts.name: Energy sub-levels and atomic orbitals (s and p)
concepts.explanation: Concept of energy sub-levels within principal levels and the shapes of s and p atomic orbitals.

concepts.name: Aufbau (building-up) and electronic configurations for first 36 elements
concepts.explanation: Rules for constructing electronic configurations (building-up principle) for the first 36 elements, including electron arrangement in individual p-block orbitals and configurations of s- and p-block ions.

concepts.name: First ionisation energy: trends and exceptions
concepts.explanation: Definition of first ionisation energy, its general trends down a group and across a period for main-group elements, and common exceptions to the periodic trend (qualitative explanations).

concepts.name: Second and successive ionisation energies and evidence for energy levels
concepts.explanation: Successive ionisation energies (second, third, etc.) and how sudden large increases provide experimental evidence for electron shells/energy levels.

concepts.name: Atomic (covalent) radii and trends
concepts.explanation: Covalent atomic radius concept and explanations for general trends in values down a group and across a period for main-group elements.

concepts.name: Radioactivity: alpha, beta and gamma radiation
concepts.explanation: Nature and relative penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma radiation, with common example isotopes for each type (e.g., 241Am, 14C, 60Co).

concepts.name: Nuclear versus chemical reactions; alpha and beta emission equations
concepts.explanation: Distinction between chemical and nuclear reactions and representation of simple nuclear equations for alpha and beta emission.

concepts.name: Half-life (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Concept of radioactive half-life described qualitatively (no mathematical treatment required) and its significance for decay rates.

concepts.name: Uses of radioisotopes (examples)
concepts.explanation: Practical applications of radioisotopes, including 14C dating, 60Co in cancer treatment and food irradiation (three exemplar uses).

concepts.name: Heisenberg uncertainty principle and wave nature of the electron (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Non-mathematical introduction to the wave nature of electrons and the Heisenberg uncertainty principle as conceptual background for atomic orbitals.

concepts.name: Demonstration: reaction of lithium, sodium and potassium with water
concepts.explanation: Classroom demonstration showing the reactivity trend of alkali metals (Li, Na, K) with water to illustrate group chemical behaviour (safety noted).

concepts.name: Mandatory experiment: viewing atomic emission spectra with a spectroscope
concepts.explanation: Practical activity using a spectroscope or spectrometer to view emission spectra of elements (demonstrates line spectra and supports energy level concepts).

concepts.name: Historical development of the periodic table: Dobereiner, Newlands, Mendeleev and Moseley
concepts.explanation: Key historical contributions to the periodic table, comparison of Mendeleev's table with the modern periodic table and the role of Moseley's work.

concepts.name: Dependence of chemical properties on electronic structure
concepts.explanation: How an element's chemical behavior is determined by its electronic configuration (valence electrons, orbital filling) and how this underlies periodic trends.

concepts.name: Atomic radius, screening effect and effective nuclear charge
concepts.explanation: Definitions and relationships between atomic radius, inner-electron screening (shielding), and effective nuclear charge, and their roles in explaining trends across periods and down groups.
concepts.broader_concept: Atomic size and effective nuclear charge

concepts.name: Trends in reactivity of Groups I (alkali metals) and VII (halogens)
concepts.explanation: General trends in chemical properties (reactivity, ionization tendencies) within Group I and Group VII and explanations based on electronic structure, atomic radius and screening.

concepts.name: Flame tests for metal ions (Li, Na, K, Ba, Sr, Cu)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative laboratory test using characteristic flame colors to identify specific metal ions (Li+, Na+, K+, Ba2+, Sr2+, Cu2+) via electronic excitation and emission.
concepts.broader_concept: Qualitative metal ion identification by flame emission

concepts.name: Oxidation and reduction (electron-transfer definitions)
concepts.explanation: Definitions of oxidation as loss of electrons and reduction as gain of electrons, with simple examples (e.g., Na with Cl2, Mg with O2, Zn with Cu2+).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Oxidising and reducing agents
concepts.explanation: Identification and role of oxidising agents (species that accept electrons) and reducing agents (species that donate electrons) in redox reactions.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Writing redox half-equations
concepts.explanation: Construction and balancing of half-equations for oxidation and reduction steps (electron transfer portions) in redox and electrolysis processes.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrochemical series (activity series of metals)
concepts.explanation: Arrangement of metals in order of their tendency to be oxidised (lose electrons); use to predict displacement reactions and relative reactivity.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Displacement reactions of metals (e.g., Zn with Cu2+, Mg with Cu2+)
concepts.explanation: Single replacement redox reactions where a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal ion from solution; experimental examples and interpretation using the electrochemical series.
concepts.broader_concept: Metal displacement reactions and activity series
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Halogens as oxidising agents (redox reactions with bromides, iodides, Fe2+, sulfites)
