concepts.explanation: Reactions demonstrating halogens (Cl2, Br2, I2) acting as oxidants, oxidising halide ions and other reducing species; includes qualitative experimental observations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of copper sulfate with copper electrodes
concepts.explanation: Electrolysis experiment where copper electrodes in CuSO4 solution demonstrate copper transfer between electrodes; use of half-equations to explain metal deposition and dissolution (basis for purification/electroplating).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of acidified water with inert electrodes
concepts.explanation: Electrolysis of aqueous acidified water using inert electrodes to produce hydrogen and oxygen gases; interpretation using half-equations and ion movement.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Demonstrations of electrolysis using indicators (aqueous Na2SO4 and KI)
concepts.explanation: Class demonstrations showing ionic movement and pH change (universal indicator with Na2SO4) and oxidation of iodide (phenolphthalein with KI) during electrolysis to visualise processes.
concepts.broader_concept: Visual demonstrations of electrolysis and ionic migration
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Applications of redox and electrochemistry (rusting, electroplating, copper purification, water treatment, metal extraction)
concepts.explanation: Practical and social applications: corrosion (rusting), electroplating (chrome/nickel plating, cutlery), electrolytic purification of copper, use of scrap iron to extract copper, and chlorine-based swimming-pool treatment.
concepts.broader_concept: Practical applications of redox and electrochemistry
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Octet rule and its limitations
concepts.explanation: The tendency of atoms to gain, lose or share electrons to attain a noble-gas (8-electron) valence shell and common exceptions (expanded octets, electron-deficient species, odd-electron molecules).

concepts.name: Ionic bonding (electron transfer)
concepts.explanation: Bond formation by transfer of electrons from one atom to another producing oppositely charged ions held together by electrostatic attraction.

concepts.name: Valency explained by attainment of a stable electronic structure
concepts.explanation: Valency defined as the combining capacity of an element based on electrons gained, lost or shared to achieve a stable electronic configuration (used to predict ratios in compounds).

concepts.name: Predicting formulas of simple binary compounds using the octet rule
concepts.explanation: Use the octet rule and valencies to predict empirical formulas of binary compounds of the first 36 elements (excluding d‑block) and related simple salts.

concepts.name: Simple chemical formula notation
concepts.explanation: Writing chemical formulas using element symbols and subscripts to indicate numbers of atoms in simple compounds (interpreting and constructing basic formulas).

concepts.name: Dot-and-cross diagrams for ionic compounds
concepts.explanation: Representation of ionic bonding by showing valence electrons for each atom (dots/crosses) to illustrate electron transfer and resulting ions.

concepts.name: Sodium chloride crystal lattice structure
concepts.explanation: The NaCl ionic crystal arrangement (each ion coordinated by oppositely charged ions in a cubic lattice; typical coordination number and packing), used to illustrate ionic solids.

concepts.name: Model examination of NaCl crystal (mandatory experiment)
concepts.explanation: Practical activity to examine or build a model of the NaCl crystal lattice to visualize ionic packing and relate structure to properties (syllabus mandatory ionic experiment).

concepts.name: Characteristics of ionic substances
concepts.explanation: Key physical and chemical properties of ionic compounds (high melting/boiling points, electrical conductivity when molten or in solution, solubility patterns, brittleness).

concepts.name: Common polyatomic ions and salts (OH-, CO3^2-, NO3-, HCO3-, SO3^2-, SO4^2-)
concepts.explanation: Formulas and charges of frequently encountered polyatomic ions (hydroxide, carbonate, nitrate, hydrogencarbonate, sulfite, sulfate) and their role in forming salts (hydroxides, carbonates, nitrates, hydrogencarbonates, sulfites, sulfates).

concepts.name: Variable valency of selected transition elements (Cu, Fe, Cr, Mn)
concepts.explanation: The phenomenon of multiple common oxidation states in transition metals (examples and common states for Cu, Fe, Cr, Mn) and implications for compound formulas and naming.
concepts.broader_concept: Variable oxidation states of transition metals

concepts.name: Noble gas electron configurations and uses (He, Ar)
concepts.explanation: Noble gases have complete valence shells leading to chemical inertness; practical uses of helium and argon that exploit this inactivity (e.g., inert atmospheres, lighting, cryogenics).

concepts.name: Covalent bonding
concepts.explanation: Chemical bond formed by the sharing of pairs of electrons between nonmetal atoms to form molecules.

concepts.name: Sigma and pi bonding
concepts.explanation: Distinct types of covalent overlap: sigma (σ) bonds formed by head-on overlap of orbitals and pi (π) bonds formed by side-by-side overlap, important for multiple bonds and molecular geometry.

concepts.name: Polar and non-polar covalent bonding
concepts.explanation: Covalent bonds in which electron sharing is unequal (polar) or equal (non‑polar), determined by differences in electronegativity and molecular geometry.

concepts.name: Representation of covalent bonds using dot-and-cross diagrams
concepts.explanation: A pictorial method showing valence electrons of atoms as dots and crosses to illustrate shared electron pairs in covalent molecules.

concepts.name: Molecules and molecular scale (minute size of molecules)
concepts.explanation: The concept that substances can be composed of discrete, extremely small particles called molecules, and an appreciation of their minute scale relative to everyday objects.

concepts.name: Characteristics of covalent substances
concepts.explanation: Typical physical properties of covalent compounds, such as low electrical conductivity, variable solubility, and generally lower melting/boiling points compared to ionic solids (dependent on intermolecular forces).

concepts.name: Polarity test for liquids using a charged plastic rod
concepts.explanation: A simple qualitative test where a charged rod attracts polar liquids or induces movement in polarizable droplets, used to demonstrate molecular polarity.

concepts.name: Use of salt tablets to replace electrolytes
concepts.explanation: Application of ionic salts in everyday life where salt tablets provide sodium and chloride ions to replace electrolytes lost through sweating.

concepts.name: Electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) theory
concepts.explanation: Model that predicts molecular geometry by assuming electron pairs (bonding and lone pairs) around a central atom repel each other and adopt arrangements minimizing repulsion.

concepts.name: Shapes of molecules (ABn up to four electron pairs) and bond angles
concepts.explanation: Specific molecular geometries for species of type ABn with up to four electron pairs (linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal pyramidal, bent) and their characteristic bond angles.

concepts.name: Electronegativity and periodic trends
concepts.explanation: Concept of electronegativity, its general variation down a group (decrease) and across a period (increase), and using electronegativity differences to predict bond polarity and approximate bond type.

concepts.name: Intermolecular forces (van der Waals/London, dipole–dipole, hydrogen bonding)
concepts.explanation: The three main types of attractive forces between molecules: London dispersion (induced dipoles), dipole–dipole interactions between polar molecules, and specific strong hydrogen bonding involving N–H, O–H or F–H.

concepts.name: Effect of intermolecular forces on boiling point
concepts.explanation: How the strength and type of intermolecular forces in covalent substances determine relative boiling points (stronger IMFs → higher boiling point).

concepts.name: Comparative boiling-point examples illustrating IMFs
concepts.explanation: Use of specific molecule pairs (H2 vs O2; C2H4 vs HCHO; H2O vs H2S) to illustrate how molecular mass, polarity and hydrogen bonding affect boiling points.

concepts.name: Relationship between molecular symmetry and polarity
concepts.explanation: How molecular symmetry determines whether bond dipoles cancel or produce an overall molecular dipole (polarity) without requiring dipole moment calculations.

concepts.name: Distinction between intramolecular bonding and intermolecular forces
concepts.explanation: Clarify difference between strong bonds holding atoms together within molecules (covalent, ionic, metallic) and weaker forces acting between separate molecules (IMFs).

concepts.name: Use of physical models or balloons to illustrate molecular shape
concepts.explanation: Pedagogical technique using ball-and-stick models, space-fill models or balloons to visualize electron pair geometry and molecular shapes.

concepts.name: Oxidation numbers: rules and redox as changes in oxidation number
concepts.explanation: Definition and rules for assigning oxidation numbers (with peroxide excluded except H2O2) and describing oxidation/reduction as increases/decreases in oxidation number.

concepts.name: Calculation of oxidation numbers for transition metals and use in nomenclature
concepts.explanation: Methods to determine oxidation numbers of transition metals in compounds and applying those oxidation states in naming transition metal compounds.
concepts.broader_concept: Transition metal oxidation states and nomenclature

concepts.name: Examples of oxidising and reducing agents (bleach NaOCl; SO2)
concepts.explanation: Applied examples showing NaOCl (bleaches) as oxidising agents and SO2 as a reducing agent, illustrating redox behavior in common substances.

concepts.name: Qualitative tests for anions in aqueous solution
concepts.explanation: Laboratory tests and observational procedures to identify common anions: chloride, carbonate, nitrate, sulfate, phosphate, sulfite and hydrogencarbonate in aqueous solutions.

concepts.name: The mole (Avogadro constant and SI unit for amount of substance)
concepts.explanation: Definition of the mole as the SI unit for amount of substance and the Avogadro constant (number of particles in one mole); use of the concept in counting atoms, molecules and particles.

concepts.name: Conversions between moles, mass, volume and number of particles
concepts.explanation: Calculations converting moles to grams, litres (of gas) at given conditions or at s.t.p., and to number of particles (and the reverse), using molar mass, molar volume and Avogadro constant.

concepts.name: Empirical and molecular formulas
concepts.explanation: Determination of empirical formula from percentage composition or masses; deriving molecular formula from empirical formula plus relative molecular mass (examples include glucose and urea).

concepts.name: Balancing chemical equations and stoichiometric calculations
concepts.explanation: Writing and balancing chemical equations and performing quantitative calculations based on balanced equations using the mole concept (including mass and volume relationships).

concepts.name: Calculations involving an excess of one reactant
concepts.explanation: Stoichiometric calculations where one reactant is in excess: identifying limiting quantities, calculating amounts of product and leftover reagent.

concepts.name: Percentage yield calculations
concepts.explanation: Calculating theoretical yield from stoichiometry and actual yield from experiment to determine percentage yield; simple examples.

concepts.name: Balancing redox equations (ionic equations, spectators ignored)
concepts.explanation: Balancing oxidation–reduction equations in ionic form, excluding spectator ions; method for balancing electron transfer.

concepts.name: Classical gas laws (Boyle's, Charles's, Gay-Lussac's and Avogadro's laws)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative and simple quantitative statements of Boyle's law, Charles's law, Gay-Lussac's law of combining volumes and Avogadro's law; relationships between pressure, volume and temperature.

concepts.name: Combined gas law and simple gas volume corrections
concepts.explanation: Use of combined gas law relationships (P1V1 = P2V2 etc.) for problems and correcting gas volumes to standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.).

concepts.name: Ideal gas equation PV = nRT and kinetic theory (non-mathematical)
concepts.explanation: The ideal gas law (including units: Pa, m³, K) and the kinetic theory assumptions that lead to ideal behaviour; reasons for deviations from ideal gas behaviour (qualitative).
concepts.broader_concept: Ideal Gas Law and Kinetic Theory

concepts.name: Standard temperature and pressure (s.t.p.) and molar volume at s.t.p.
concepts.explanation: Definition of standard temperature and pressure and the molar volume of an ideal gas at s.t.p.; use in converting between gas volume and moles.

concepts.name: Determination of relative molecular mass by mass spectrometer (simple treatment)
concepts.explanation: Using mass spectrometry in a basic way to determine relative molecular mass; simple description of the experimental determination (interpretation of spectra not required).

concepts.name: Determination of relative molecular mass of a volatile liquid (laboratory method)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory experiment to determine Mr of a volatile liquid using a conical flask or gas syringe method (measurements of mass and gas volume/pressure/temperature).

concepts.name: Concentration units and calculations (molarity, g L⁻¹, % w/v, % v/v, % w/w)
concepts.explanation: Definitions and interconversion of common concentration units including mol L⁻¹ (molarity), grams per litre and percentage concentrations; calculating moles from molarity and volume.

concepts.name: Dilution and preparation of standard solutions (including primary standards)
concepts.explanation: Preparation and use of primary standards and standard solutions; calculation of concentration changes on dilution and practical preparation steps.

concepts.name: Neutralisation and acid–base theories (Arrhenius and Brønsted–Lowry) with conjugate pairs
concepts.explanation: Concept of neutralisation (formation of a salt), Arrhenius and Brønsted–Lowry definitions for aqueous systems, and identification of conjugate acid–base pairs.

concepts.name: Everyday acids, bases and applications of neutralisation
concepts.explanation: Examples of common household acids and bases, and practical applications of neutralisation such as use of lime in agriculture and antacids for indigestion.

concepts.name: Apparatus used in volumetric analysis
concepts.explanation: Identification and correct use of common titration glassware and equipment (burette, pipette, volumetric flask, conical flask, wash bottle, indicators, standard solids/reagents).

concepts.name: Acid–base titrations
concepts.explanation: Titration methods for quantitative determination of acid or base concentration using acid–base neutralisation reactions and suitable indicators or pH measurement.

concepts.name: Preparation of a standard solution of sodium carbonate (primary standard)
concepts.explanation: Making a primary-standard solution by accurately weighing anhydrous/known composition sodium carbonate, dissolving to a known volume in a volumetric flask to produce a solution of known molarity.

concepts.name: Standardisation of hydrochloric acid using sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Determining the exact concentration of an HCl solution by titration against a known-concentration sodium carbonate primary standard and calculating molarity from titre data and stoichiometry.

concepts.name: Formula method for volumetric calculations
concepts.explanation: Using memorised titration formulae such as C1V1 = C2V2 (adjusted for stoichiometric ratios) to calculate concentrations and amounts from titration data.

concepts.name: First-principles titration calculations
concepts.explanation: Deriving quantities from fundamental relationships (moles = concentration × volume, using balanced chemical equations for mole ratios) rather than relying on memorised shortcut formulae.

concepts.name: Use of balanced chemical equations in titration calculations
concepts.explanation: Applying balanced reaction equations to determine stoichiometric mole ratios between analyte and titrant for accurate quantitative calculations in titrations.

concepts.name: Calculation of relative molecular mass and water of crystallisation from titration data
concepts.explanation: Determining a compound's formula mass or number of waters of crystallisation by combining titration-derived mole quantities with mass measurements to solve for molecular or hydration formulae.
concepts.broader_concept: Quantitative determination of composition by titration

concepts.name: Potassium manganate(VII) / ammonium iron(II) sulfate titration (KMnO4 vs Fe2+)
concepts.explanation: Redox titration in which manganate(VII) oxidises Fe2+ to Fe3+; self-indicating endpoint occurs when excess MnO4- gives a pink colour—used to determine iron content or Fe2+ concentration.

concepts.name: Iodine / thiosulfate titration
concepts.explanation: Indirect redox titration where iodine (I2) is titrated with sodium thiosulfate; commonly used after generation of I2 by oxidising iodide or for halogen/oxidiser quantification.

concepts.name: Determination of the concentration of ethanoic acid in vinegar
concepts.explanation: Quantitative acid analysis by titration (typically acid–base titration against standardized NaOH) to calculate percentage or molarity of ethanoic acid in a vinegar sample.

concepts.name: Determination of the amount of iron in an iron tablet
concepts.explanation: Quantifying iron content by dissolving tablet, converting iron to an appropriate oxidation state, and performing a redox titration (e.g., with KMnO4 or via Fe2+/Fe3+ methods) to calculate mass percent.

concepts.name: Determination of percentage (w/v) of hypochlorite in bleach
concepts.explanation: Measuring oxidising-agent concentration in bleach by titration (commonly iodine/thiosulfate after acidification) to calculate percent weight/volume of available hypochlorite.

concepts.name: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
concepts.explanation: Classification of chemical reactions (and changes of state) by whether they release or absorb heat; sign convention for ΔH.

concepts.name: Heat of combustion
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change when one mole of a substance combusts completely in oxygen; used to compare fuel energy content.

concepts.name: Hess's law
concepts.explanation: Enthalpy change for a reaction is path-independent and can be determined from a series of steps whose enthalpies are known.

concepts.name: Bond energy (concept) and illustrative C–H calculation
concepts.explanation: Average energy required to break a particular type of bond; concept used to rationalize heats of reaction and illustrated by calculating the C–H bond energy in methane.

concepts.name: Determination of heat of reaction (HCl + NaOH calorimetry)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory calorimetry experiment measuring temperature change on neutralization to determine heat of reaction.

concepts.name: Combustion of alkanes and hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Oxidation reactions of alkanes and other hydrocarbons producing CO2, H2O (and sometimes CO or soot), with associated heat release.

concepts.name: Heat of formation
concepts.explanation: Standard enthalpy change for forming one mole of a compound from its elements in their standard states; used in reaction enthalpy calculations.

concepts.name: Calculations of reaction enthalpies using heats of formation
concepts.explanation: Using standard heats of formation of reactants and products to compute ΔH for a reaction via ΣΔHf(products) − ΣΔHf(reactants).

concepts.name: Octane number and auto-ignition (engine knocking)
concepts.explanation: A measure of a petrol's resistance to auto-ignition (knocking); higher octane indicates less tendency to knock.

concepts.name: Structural effects on octane number (chain length, branching, cyclicity)
concepts.explanation: How molecular structure—longer chain length, degree of branching, and presence of rings—affects tendency to auto-ignite and thus octane rating.

concepts.name: Refinery processes to improve octane: isomerisation, dehydrocyclisation, catalytic cracking
concepts.explanation: Industrial transformations that convert low-octane hydrocarbons to higher-octane isomers or aromatic/cyclic compounds using catalysts and thermal processes.

concepts.name: Addition of mercaptans to natural gas (odorization)
concepts.explanation: Deliberate addition of sulfur-containing compounds (mercaptans) to otherwise odorless gases to provide a detectable smell for leak safety.

concepts.name: Tests for unsaturation: bromine water and acidified potassium manganate(VII)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative tests for C=C or C≡C bonds: decolorization of bromine water and oxidative bleaching/colour change of acidified KMnO4.

concepts.name: Industrial manufacture of hydrogen (electrolysis and steam reforming)
concepts.explanation: Two principal production routes: electrolysis of water (electrical energy input) and steam reforming of natural gas (catalytic reaction with steam).

concepts.name: Methane sources, hazards and greenhouse impact
concepts.explanation: Origins of methane (coal, natural gas, decomposition of waste/vegetation), hazards in mines/slurry pits/refuse dumps, and role as a greenhouse gas.
concepts.broader_concept: Sources and environmental effects of methane

concepts.name: Solubility properties of small hydrocarbons (qualitative)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative understanding that small hydrocarbons (e.g., methane, ethene, ethyne, methylbenzene) are insoluble in water but soluble in non-polar solvents.

concepts.name: Homologous series, nomenclature and structural isomerism for small hydrocarbons
concepts.explanation: Classification and systematic naming of alkanes, alkenes and alkynes; drawing structural formulas and structural isomers for alkanes to C-5 and alkenes to C-4.

concepts.name: Structure of benzene and simple aromatics (methylbenzene, ethylbenzene)
concepts.explanation: Representation and recognition of benzene and substituted benzenes (toluene, ethylbenzene) as examples of aromatic compounds with characteristic stability and properties.

concepts.name: Calorific value (kilogram calorific values) of fuels and foods
concepts.explanation: Energy content of fuels and foods expressed per unit mass (kJ kg−1 or similar) and its determination/use with calorimetric methods.

concepts.name: Rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: Definition and concept of how fast reactants are converted to products, usually expressed as change in concentration or amount per unit time.

concepts.name: Average vs instantaneous rate
concepts.explanation: Distinction between average reaction rate over a time interval and instantaneous rate at a specific moment in time.

concepts.name: Calculation of instantaneous rate from graphs
concepts.explanation: Procedure for determining the instantaneous rate of reaction by finding the slope of the concentration‑vs‑time curve at a particular time (tangent method).

concepts.name: Plotting and interpretation of reaction rate graphs (mandatory experiment)
concepts.explanation: Experimental activity involving measurement of concentration or amount versus time, plotting the data, and performing simple interpretation of reaction rate graphs.

concepts.name: Factors affecting rate of reaction
concepts.explanation: Identification and study of variables that influence reaction rates (e.g., concentration, temperature, catalysts, surface area, pressure for gases) as a unit concept.

concepts.name: Activation energy and temperature dependence (reaction profile diagrams)
concepts.explanation: Definition of activation energy; how temperature influences reaction rate explained with reaction energy profile diagrams and the Arrhenius concept (higher temperature increases fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Ea).

concepts.name: Catalysts and lowering of activation energy
concepts.explanation: Role of catalysts in increasing reaction rate by providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy, without being consumed in the overall reaction.

concepts.name: Mechanisms of catalysis: adsorption and intermediate formation
concepts.explanation: Surface adsorption (reactants adsorb on catalyst surface) and intermediate formation (reaction proceeds via surface-bound intermediates) as mechanistic models explaining heterogeneous catalysis.

concepts.name: Concentration effect on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How changing reactant concentration alters frequency of effective collisions and thus the reaction rate; qualitative and simple quantitative treatment (rate laws at basic level).

concepts.name: Particle size (surface area) effect on reaction rate
concepts.explanation: Influence of particle size (and resulting surface area) on reaction rate for heterogeneous reactions: smaller particles increase available surface area and collision probability at surfaces.

concepts.name: Nature of reactants and reaction rate
concepts.explanation: How intrinsic chemical properties of reactants (bond types, molecular complexity, phase, polarity) affect rate by altering activation energy and collision effectiveness.

concepts.name: Catalyst poisoning
concepts.explanation: Processes by which impurities or specific substances bind to catalyst active sites, reducing catalyst activity and slowing catalysed reaction rates.

concepts.name: Enzymes as biological catalysts (examples)
concepts.explanation: Enzymes produced by living cells that accelerate biochemical reactions; includes study of two illustrative enzyme examples, their specificity and catalytic behavior.

concepts.name: Catalytic converters: catalysts, reactions catalysed and environmental benefits
concepts.explanation: Composition and function of catalytic converters (e.g., Pt, Pd, Rh), the key oxidation and reduction reactions they catalyse, and their role in reducing vehicle emissions.

concepts.name: Experiment: monitoring O2 production from H2O2 using MnO2 catalyst
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to measure the rate of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide by monitoring oxygen gas evolution, using solid manganese dioxide as a heterogeneous catalyst.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental methods for measuring reaction rates

concepts.name: Experiment: effect of concentration and temperature on rate using sodium thiosulfate and hydrochloric acid
concepts.explanation: Standard classroom experiment (thiosulfate 'clock') to investigate how varying concentration and temperature affect the rate of a reaction by timing solution turbidity due to sulfur formation.
concepts.broader_concept: Experimental methods for measuring reaction rates

concepts.name: Demonstration: oxidation of methanol over hot platinum or nichrome catalyst
concepts.explanation: Teacher demonstration showing catalytic oxidation of methanol using a heated platinum or nichrome surface to illustrate heterogeneous catalysis and increased reaction rate.

concepts.name: Demonstration: oxidation of potassium sodium tartrate by H2O2 catalysed by cobalt(II) salts
concepts.explanation: Classroom demonstration of a catalysed oxidation reaction where Co(II) salts accelerate oxidation of tartrate by hydrogen peroxide, illustrating transition-metal catalysis in solution.

concepts.name: Dust explosions (effect of fine particulates on combustion rate)
concepts.explanation: Phenomenon where dispersed fine combustible particles ignite rapidly due to large surface area and high contact with oxidant, illustrating industrial hazard related to particle size and concentration.
concepts.broader_concept: Safety and hazards related to rapid reactions

concepts.name: Tetrahedral carbon geometry
concepts.explanation: The sp3-hybridized carbon atom bonded to four substituents adopts a tetrahedral geometry (bond angles ~109.5°), characteristic of saturated organic compounds.

concepts.name: Alkanes: structure and nomenclature (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons with single C–C bonds; includes systematic naming and structural formulas for methane, ethane, propane and butane and their isomers.

concepts.name: Chloroalkanes (haloalkanes) up to C4
concepts.explanation: Alkanes bearing chlorine substituents: structure, naming (up to four carbons) and basic physical property trends introduced as a halogenated alkane functional group.

concepts.name: Alcohol functional group: primary vs secondary (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Structure and nomenclature of alcohols up to four carbons, distinguishing primary and secondary alcohols by the carbon to which the –OH is attached and noting their basic physical properties and solubility trends.

concepts.name: Alkenes: C=C double bond structure and nomenclature (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Unsaturated hydrocarbons containing a carbon–carbon double bond; includes structure, naming for up to four carbons, and the non‑polar nature of the C=C bond.

concepts.name: Aldehyde functional group (carbonyl polarity) up to C4
concepts.explanation: Structure and naming of aldehydes (R–CHO) up to four carbons, emphasizing the polar C=O bond and its influence on physical properties such as solubility.

concepts.name: Ketone functional group up to C4
concepts.explanation: Structure and nomenclature of ketones (R–CO–R') up to four carbons and discussion of their physical properties (polarity, solubility trends).

concepts.name: Carboxylic acids: structure, nomenclature and properties (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Structure and naming of carboxylic acids (R–COOH) up to four carbons, emphasizing the polar/acidic nature of the carboxyl group and effects on physical state and solubility.

concepts.name: Esters: structure, nomenclature and properties (up to C4)
concepts.explanation: Structural formulae and naming of simple esters up to four carbons, with emphasis on their physical properties, characteristic aromas, and occurrence as natural fats (triglycerides).

concepts.name: Aromaticity in benzene: delocalized pi bonding and the circle representation
concepts.explanation: The concept that benzene has a cyclic system of delocalized pi electrons (intermediate bond order between single and double); represented by a circle in the ring and explained by sigma framework plus delocalized pi bonding.

concepts.name: Aromatic stability and relative reactivity (benzene vs alkenes)
concepts.explanation: Aromatic compounds (e.g., benzene) are comparatively unreactive toward addition reactions because delocalized pi-electron stabilization is lost by addition; explains preference for substitution in aromatics.

concepts.name: Electrophilic addition reactions of alkenes (H2, Cl2, Br2, HCl, H2O)
concepts.explanation: Addition reactions where reagents add across C=C bonds (hydrogenation, halogenation, hydrohalogenation, hydration), producing saturated products; students should be able to write balanced structural equations.

concepts.name: Ionic (electrophilic) addition mechanism to ethene
concepts.explanation: The stepwise mechanistic description of electrophilic addition to ethene (formation of carbocation/bridged intermediate and nucleophilic attack) exemplified for reagents like HCl, Br2 and Cl2.

concepts.name: Experimental evidence for ionic addition (bromine water + NaCl with ethene)
concepts.explanation: Observation that ethene reacting with bromine water containing NaCl yields products such as 2-bromoethanol, 1-bromo-2-chloroethane and 1,2-dibromoethane, supporting ionic addition pathways and multiple possible additions.

concepts.name: Polymerisation of alkenes (addition polymerisation of ethene and propene)
concepts.explanation: Formation of high molecular weight polymers by repeated addition of alkene monomers (chain-growth polymerisation) to form polyethylene and polypropylene; mechanism details not required beyond concept.

concepts.name: Free radical halogenation of alkanes (monochlorination mechanism)
concepts.explanation: Chain mechanism for alkane halogenation involving initiation (radical formation, e.g., by UV), propagation (hydrogen abstraction and halogen radical reactions) and termination, illustrated by monochlorination of methane/ethane.

concepts.name: Evidence for free radical substitution mechanism
concepts.explanation: Key observations supporting a radical chain mechanism include initiation by ultraviolet light (even briefly), formation of trace higher alkanes in some chlorinations, and acceleration by radical sources (e.g., tetraethyllead).

concepts.name: Solubility of organic compounds in water vs non‑polar solvents (qualitative solubility experiments)
concepts.explanation: Qualitative experiments comparing solubility of small organics (e.g., methanol, butan-1-ol, ethanal, propanone, ethanoic acid, ethyl ethanoate, methylbenzene) in water and cyclohexane to illustrate polarity, hydrogen bonding and solute–solvent interactions.
concepts.broader_concept: Physical properties and solubility of organic molecules

concepts.name: Fermentation as a source of ethanol
concepts.explanation: Biochemical conversion of sugars to ethanol and CO2 by yeast (fermentation) as an industrial and laboratory source of ethanol, with applications in brewing and distilling.
concepts.broader_concept: Biochemical and industrial sources of organic compounds

concepts.name: Hydrogenation of vegetable oils (industrial application)
concepts.explanation: Catalytic addition of hydrogen to unsaturated C=C bonds in vegetable oils to produce saturated or partially hydrogenated fats; an applied example of alkene hydrogenation with industrial importance.

concepts.name: Organic synthesis principles (bond breaking and bond forming; multi-step schemes)
concepts.explanation: Fundamental idea that organic synthesis proceeds via specific bond-breaking and bond-forming steps; practice in planning reaction schemes of up to three conversions using familiar reactions.

concepts.name: Esterification (formation of esters from alcohols and carboxylic acids)
concepts.explanation: Acid-catalysed condensation reaction between an alcohol and a carboxylic acid producing an ester and water; understanding reagents, conditions and product identification.

concepts.name: Base hydrolysis of esters (saponification)
concepts.explanation: Nucleophilic attack of hydroxide on an ester leading to cleavage to give a carboxylate salt and an alcohol; industrial relevance in soap manufacture.

concepts.name: Soap manufacture (industrial saponification)
concepts.explanation: Industrial process using base hydrolysis of triglyceride esters to produce soap (alkali metal salts of fatty acids) and glycerol; includes structures of reactants and products.

concepts.name: Dehydration of alcohols (elimination reactions)
concepts.explanation: Acid-catalysed elimination of water from alcohols to form alkenes (E1/E2 type behaviour at this level), conditions and product considerations.

concepts.name: Oxidation of primary alcohols with KMnO4 or Na2Cr2O7 (to aldehydes and acids)
concepts.explanation: Oxidation sequence where primary alcohols are oxidised first to aldehydes then to carboxylic acids under strong oxidising conditions; half-equations may be written for oxidants.

concepts.name: Oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids (half-equations)
concepts.explanation: Conversion of aldehydes to carboxylic acids by oxidising agents, with focus on writing relevant half-equations for oxidant/redox changes.

concepts.name: Ketone resistance to oxidation
concepts.explanation: Observation and principle that ketones are generally not readily oxidised under mild oxidising conditions that oxidise alcohols and aldehydes.

concepts.name: Reduction of carbonyl compounds using H2 with Ni catalyst
concepts.explanation: Catalytic hydrogenation of aldehydes and ketones to the corresponding alcohols using hydrogen gas and a nickel catalyst.

concepts.name: Reaction of alcohols with sodium (formation of alkoxides and hydrogen gas)
concepts.explanation: Alcohols react with sodium metal to form alkoxide salts and liberate hydrogen gas; demonstrates acidic character of alcohol OH (relative to water).

concepts.name: Acidic nature of the carboxylic acid group
concepts.explanation: Carboxylic acids donate a proton from the -COOH group, forming carboxylate ions; teaching includes pKa concept at a basic level and typical reactions with bases and metals.
concepts.broader_concept: Acid-Base Behaviour of Organic Functional Groups

concepts.name: Reactions of carboxylic acids with magnesium, sodium hydroxide and sodium carbonate
concepts.explanation: Typical reactions: acid + metal (e.g., Mg) -> salt + H2; acid + NaOH -> salt + water (neutralisation); acid + Na2CO3 -> salt + CO2 + water (carbonate reaction).

concepts.name: PVC synthesis from ethene (multi-step polymer synthesis route)
concepts.explanation: Multi-step industrial/organic synthesis route converting ethene to poly(chloroethene) (PVC), requiring understanding of intermediate steps and polymerisation principles (structures and route required).

concepts.name: Chromatography techniques for organic compounds (separation and analysis)
concepts.explanation: Practical separation and identification methods (e.g., thin-layer chromatography) for organic mixtures, including interpretation of results and Rf values.

concepts.name: Calculation of percentage yield from a balanced equation (practical data analysis)
concepts.explanation: Use of stoichiometry and experimental masses to calculate theoretical yield and percentage yield; practiced in laboratory experiments.

concepts.name: Combustion of alcohols (organic combustion reactions)
concepts.explanation: Complete combustion of alcohols producing CO2 and H2O; involves balanced equation practice and discussion of energy release and flammability.

concepts.name: Ethanal formation in the metabolism of ethanol
concepts.explanation: Biochemical oxidation of ethanol to ethanal (acetaldehyde) in the human body (relevance to toxicology and metabolism).

concepts.name: Non-flammability of fully halogenated alkanes
concepts.explanation: Property that fully halogenated alkanes resist combustion due to absence of hydrogen atoms and stabilising effects of halogens; relevance to flame retardants and fire suppression.
concepts.broader_concept: Halogenated Organic Compounds and Fire Safety

concepts.name: Flame retardants and fire extinguishers (applications of organic chemistry)
concepts.explanation: Use of certain halogenated compounds and other chemicals as flame retardants or in fire extinguishing agents; discussion of chemical principles and social/environmental implications.
concepts.broader_concept: Applications of Halogenated Organics in Fire Safety

concepts.name: Chromatography (principles: mobile and stationary phases)
concepts.explanation: Principle of chromatographic separation where a mobile phase carrying a mixture moves in contact with a selectively adsorbent stationary phase, allowing components to separate based on differing affinities.

concepts.name: Thin-layer chromatography (TLC) and forensic dye separation
concepts.explanation: Practical chromatographic technique using a thin adsorbent layer on a plate to separate small organic mixtures; used to separate and compare dyes extracted from fibres in forensic analysis.

concepts.name: Rf value (TLC retention factor)
concepts.explanation: Quantitative measure in TLC defined as distance travelled by a compound divided by distance travelled by the solvent front; used for comparing and identifying compounds under fixed conditions.

concepts.name: Solvent extraction (liquid-liquid extraction)
concepts.explanation: Technique for separating compounds based on their relative solubilities in two immiscible liquids (typically aqueous and organic solvents), used to isolate organic products from mixtures.

concepts.name: Steam distillation
concepts.explanation: Distillation method for separating temperature-sensitive or immiscible volatile organic compounds by co-distillation with water vapor, allowing isolation below their normal boiling points.

concepts.name: Mass spectrometry (MS) — basic analytical use
concepts.explanation: Analytical technique that measures mass-to-charge ratios of ionized fragments to provide molecular weight information and aid identification of organic compounds (basic principles and role in analysis).

concepts.name: Infrared (IR) absorption spectroscopy (fingerprinting)
concepts.explanation: Spectroscopic method where organic molecules absorb infrared radiation at characteristic frequencies; used as a 'fingerprint' for identifying functional groups and confirming compound identity.

concepts.name: Ultraviolet (UV) absorption spectroscopy (quantitative analysis)
concepts.explanation: Technique measuring absorption of ultraviolet light by organic compounds; used quantitatively (e.g., via Beer–Lambert relationship) to determine concentrations of UV-absorbing species.

concepts.name: Recrystallisation of benzoic acid and melting point determination
concepts.explanation: Purification of benzoic acid by dissolving in hot solvent, filtering, cooling to recrystallise, drying crystals, and determining purity via melting point measurement.

concepts.name: Chromatographic separation of a mixture of indicators (paper/TLC/column)
concepts.explanation: Use of paper chromatography, thin-layer chromatography or column chromatography to separate components of an indicator mixture, including concepts of stationary/mobile phases and Rf values for identification.

concepts.name: Steam distillation extraction of clove oil (essential oil extraction)
concepts.explanation: Isolation of volatile organic compounds (e.g., clove oil) from plant material by steam distillation, separating immiscible oil from aqueous distillate and recovering the oil.
concepts.broader_concept: Essential oil extraction by steam distillation

concepts.name: Preparation of soap (saponification)
concepts.explanation: Formation of soap by alkaline hydrolysis (saponification) of fats or oils with strong base, yielding glycerol and carboxylate salts (soap).

concepts.name: Preparation and properties of ethene: combustion and tests for unsaturation
concepts.explanation: Laboratory preparation of ethene and investigation of its combustion behavior and unsaturation tests using decolourisation of bromine water and oxidation with acidified potassium manganate(VII).
concepts.broader_concept: Alkene properties and tests for unsaturation

concepts.name: Preparation and reactions of ethanal (aldehyde tests)
concepts.explanation: Preparation of ethanal and its characteristic reactions: oxidation by acidified potassium manganate(VII), reduction/confirmation with Fehling's reagent (Fehling's test) and ammoniacal silver nitrate (Tollens' test).

concepts.name: Preparation and reactions of ethanoic acid (acid-carbonate, acid-metal, esterification)
concepts.explanation: Preparation of ethanoic acid and limited properties: reaction with sodium carbonate (CO2 evolution), with magnesium (hydrogen evolution), and with ethanol (esterification to give ethyl ethanoate).

concepts.name: Reversible reactions and dynamic chemical equilibrium
concepts.explanation: A reversible reaction reaches a dynamic equilibrium when the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction and macroscopic properties remain constant.

concepts.name: Equilibrium law and equilibrium constant (Kc)
concepts.explanation: The equilibrium law expresses the relationship between concentrations of reactants and products at equilibrium; the equilibrium constant Kc is the ratio of product concentration terms to reactant concentration terms (each raised to their stoichiometric coefficients) for reactions in solution.

concepts.name: Calculations involving equilibrium constants (Kc)
concepts.explanation: Techniques for calculating Kc from equilibrium concentrations and for using Kc to determine equilibrium concentrations (including setting up ICE tables and solving for unknowns).

concepts.name: Effect of temperature changes on equilibrium position and Kc
concepts.explanation: How changing temperature shifts equilibrium (exothermic reactions shift left when temperature increases, endothermic shift right) and alters the value of Kc depending on reaction enthalpy.

concepts.name: Effect of pressure (and volume) changes on gaseous equilibria
concepts.explanation: How changes in pressure or volume affect equilibria involving gases, with the system shifting toward the side with fewer moles of gas when pressure increases (or volume decreases).

concepts.name: CoCl4(2-) / [Co(H2O)6]2+ colour-change equilibrium demonstration
concepts.explanation: A classroom experiment using the equilibrium between tetrahedral CoCl4(2-) (blue) and hexaaquacobalt(II) [Co(H2O)6]2+ (pink) to demonstrate effects of temperature and chloride concentration on an equilibrium mixture.

concepts.name: Chromate/dichromate (Cr2O7(2-) ⇌ CrO4(2-)) equilibrium demonstration with H2O2
concepts.explanation: An experiment using interconversion between dichromate and chromate (orange/yellow) in the presence of hydrogen peroxide and H+ to illustrate shifts in equilibrium caused by concentration changes (and pH).

concepts.name: Iron(III) thiocyanate equilibrium (Fe3+ + SCN- ⇌ FeSCN2+) demonstration
concepts.explanation: A colourimetric equilibrium experiment forming the red FeSCN2+ complex used to demonstrate effects of concentration changes on equilibrium position and to determine an equilibrium constant experimentally.

concepts.name: Haber process as an industrial application of Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.explanation: Application of Le Chatelier's principle to ammonia synthesis (N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3) where pressure, temperature, and catalysts are optimised to favour yield while considering kinetics and equilibrium.

concepts.name: Catalytic oxidation of sulfur dioxide to sulfur trioxide (Contact process) application of Le Chatelier's principle
concepts.explanation: Industrial oxidation of SO2 to SO3 (2SO2 + O2 ⇌ 2SO3) illustrating how pressure, temperature, and catalysts are chosen to maximise SO3 yield in accordance with Le Chatelier's principle and kinetics.

concepts.name: Self-ionisation of water and Kw
concepts.explanation: The autoionisation equilibrium H2O ⇌ H+ + OH− and the ionic product of water Kw = [H+][OH−], including temperature dependence and its use in pH calculations.

concepts.name: pH scale and limitations
concepts.explanation: Definition of pH as −log[H+] (or −log aH+), interpretation of pH values, and limitations of the pH scale (usefulness confined to dilute aqueous solutions).

concepts.name: Calculation of pH for strong acids and bases in dilute solutions
concepts.explanation: Compute [H+] (or [OH−]) and pH for dilute aqueous solutions of strong monoprotic acids and bases, including mixtures (note: mixtures of strong acids and bases not required by syllabus).

concepts.name: pH calculation for weak acids and bases (approximation method)
concepts.explanation: Estimating pH of weak acids and bases using equilibrium expressions and the common approximation that ionisation is small so the initial concentration is unchanged (ICE table with approximation).

concepts.name: Theory and choice of acid–base indicators
concepts.explanation: Principles of acid–base indicators as weak acids/bases with a visible color change around their pKa, and selecting an appropriate indicator for a titration based on expected equivalence pH.

concepts.name: Titration curves and equivalence point vs end point
concepts.explanation: Interpretation of pH vs volume titration curves, locating the equivalence point and relating it to the indicator end point and choice of indicator.

concepts.name: Temporary and permanent hardness of water
concepts.explanation: Causes of hardness (typically Ca2+ and Mg2+ salts), distinction between temporary hardness (removed by boiling due to carbonate precipitation) and permanent hardness (caused by non-carbonate salts).

concepts.name: Removal of hardness: boiling and ion exchange (deionisation)
concepts.explanation: Methods for removing hardness: boiling to precipitate bicarbonates and ion-exchange/deionisation to replace Ca2+/Mg2+ with Na+ or H+, including relative purity of deionised vs distilled water.
concepts.broader_concept: Water purification by ion exchange and thermal methods

concepts.name: EDTA complexometric titration for total hardness
concepts.explanation: Use of EDTA to titrate and estimate total hardness (Ca2+ and Mg2+) in water; principles of complex formation and the stoichiometry/balanced ionic equation for the titration.

concepts.name: Water treatment processes (sedimentation, flocculation, filtration, chlorination, fluoridation, pH adjustment)
concepts.explanation: Key physical and chemical steps used in municipal water treatment: settling (sedimentation), flocculation/coagulation, filtration, disinfection by chlorination, fluoridation for dental health, and pH adjustment.
concepts.broader_concept: Physical and chemical water treatment steps

concepts.name: Sewage treatment stages and eutrophication
concepts.explanation: Primary (screening/settlement), secondary (biological breakdown), and tertiary (nutrient reduction) sewage treatment processes and the role of nutrients (nitrates, phosphates) in eutrophication.

concepts.name: Heavy metal ion contamination and removal by precipitation
concepts.explanation: Occurrence and environmental impact of metal ions such as Pb2+, Hg2+, Cd2+ in water, and their chemical removal by precipitation reactions (e.g., sulfide or hydroxide precipitation).
concepts.broader_concept: Heavy metal water contamination and remediation

concepts.name: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) for metal analysis
concepts.explanation: Principle of AAS: measurement of absorption of light by ground-state atoms to determine concentrations of metal ions (e.g., lead, cadmium) in water samples.
concepts.broader_concept: Instrumental methods for trace metal analysis

concepts.name: pH meter (glass electrode) principle
concepts.explanation: Operation of a pH meter using a glass electrode that responds to hydrogen ion activity, including calibration and use for accurate pH determination.

concepts.name: Colorimetry principles and application to chlorine determination
concepts.explanation: Use of colorimetric methods to determine analyte concentration by measuring light absorbance at selected wavelengths; applied in estimating free chlorine in pool water or bleach.

concepts.name: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)
concepts.explanation: BOD as a measure of the amount of dissolved oxygen needed by aerobic biological organisms to break down organic material in water; used to assess organic pollution levels.

concepts.name: Estimation of dissolved oxygen by redox titration (Winkler method)
concepts.explanation: Redox titrimetric method for measuring dissolved oxygen in water (Winkler titration), involving fixation of oxygen as an oxidant and subsequent titration to quantify O2.
concepts.broader_concept: Redox titration methods for water analysis

concepts.name: Determination of total suspended and total dissolved solids (gravimetric ppm)
concepts.explanation: Laboratory procedure to measure total suspended solids (TSS) by filtration and total dissolved solids (TDS) by evaporation, reporting concentrations in parts per million (ppm).

concepts.name: Batch, continuous and semi-continuous industrial chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Classification and definition of process operation modes: batch (discrete charges and runs), continuous (steady input/output flow), and semi-continuous (hybrid operations), including their operational implications for scale-up, control, productivity and suitability for different products.

concepts.name: Feedstock (raw material) selection for industrial chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Selection and evaluation of feedstocks (raw materials) used in industrial processes, considering factors such as availability, cost, purity, compatibility with process conditions and impact on yield and downstream processing.

concepts.name: Catalyst effects on reaction rate and yield
concepts.explanation: How catalysts increase reaction rate by lowering activation energy, their impact on reaction mechanisms, selectivity, and how they can improve product yield without being consumed

concepts.name: Temperature and pressure influence on reaction rate and yield
concepts.explanation: Dependence of reaction rates on temperature (Arrhenius behavior) and the effect of pressure on gas-phase reactions and equilibria (Le Chatelier principles) that determine yield

concepts.name: Heat exchangers for energy recovery in chemical processes
concepts.explanation: Use of heat exchangers to transfer heat between process streams to reduce external energy input and operating costs, including countercurrent and shell-and-tube designs and basic heat-balance considerations

concepts.name: Separation techniques for co-products
concepts.explanation: Physical and chemical separation methods (e.g., distillation, extraction, filtration, crystallization) used to isolate desired products and co-products from reaction mixtures

concepts.name: Recycling and recovery of reactants and co-products
concepts.explanation: Process strategies for recycling unreacted feedstock and recovering useful co-products to improve atom economy, reduce raw material costs, and minimize waste

concepts.name: Wastewater treatment in chemical manufacturing
concepts.explanation: Chemical and physical treatment steps (neutralization, sedimentation, biological treatment, advanced oxidation) used to remove contaminants from industrial effluents before discharge

concepts.name: Emission control technologies for industrial gases
concepts.explanation: Methods to limit atmospheric emissions (scrubbers, catalytic converters, adsorption, flue gas treatment) and principles of monitoring and regulatory compliance

concepts.name: Quality control by analytical testing in manufacturing
concepts.explanation: Routine sampling and analytical techniques (titration, chromatography, spectroscopy) used to verify product specifications, purity, and process consistency

concepts.name: Process safety: hazard monitoring and safety features
concepts.explanation: Identification and monitoring of chemical hazards, safety systems and engineering controls (containment, alarms, ventilation), and on-site training practices to mitigate risks

concepts.name: Feedstock preparation and material handling
concepts.explanation: Preparation steps for raw materials (purification, drying, size reduction) and safe handling/storage requirements that affect downstream reaction performance

concepts.name: Cost components in chemical manufacture: fixed and variable costs
concepts.explanation: Distinction between fixed and variable costs in a chemical process and examples of cost-reduction strategies (use of catalysts, recycling, energy integration) that affect economic feasibility

concepts.name: Materials for chemical plant construction (corrosion‑resistant)
concepts.explanation: Selection and properties of materials (metals, alloys, polymers, coatings) used to construct chemical plants that are chemically unreactive and resistant to corrosion and chemical attack.

concepts.name: Corrosion mechanisms and prevention
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical and chemical processes leading to corrosion (oxidation, galvanic corrosion) and methods to prevent it (material choice, coatings, cathodic protection, inhibitors).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Water purification processes
concepts.explanation: Chemical and physical methods to provide pure water (filtration, coagulation, chlorination, disinfection, distillation, ion exchange, membrane separation).

concepts.name: Fuel chemistry and combustion
concepts.explanation: Chemical nature of fuels, combustion reactions, energy content (heats of combustion), and factors affecting efficient fuel use and emissions.

concepts.name: Metal extraction and refining (pyro‑ and hydrometallurgy)
concepts.explanation: Chemical processes for extracting and refining metals from ores (smelting, roasting, leaching, electrorefining) and basic principles of industrial metallurgy.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Surfactant chemistry and detergents
concepts.explanation: Structure, function and classifications of surfactants, micelle formation, and how detergents remove soils and oils through amphiphilic action.

concepts.name: Enzymes and biocatalysis
concepts.explanation: Structure and catalytic mechanism of enzymes, specificity, and use of enzymes as catalysts in chemical processes and industrial applications.

concepts.name: Dye and pigment chemistry
concepts.explanation: Molecular origins of colour (chromophores and auxochromes), classes of dyes, and principles of dyeing and pigment formulation.

concepts.name: Paints and coatings chemistry
concepts.explanation: Components and chemistry of paints and coatings (binders, pigments, solvents, additives), film formation, and properties like adhesion and durability.

concepts.name: Semiconductor materials and doping
concepts.explanation: Chemical nature of semiconductors, band theory basics, role of dopants, and how material chemistry controls electronic properties.

concepts.name: Liquid crystals and mesophases
concepts.explanation: Structures and types of liquid crystal phases, molecular origins of mesophases, and applications (e.g., display technology).

concepts.name: Ammonia formation (Haber process)
concepts.explanation: Industrial synthesis of ammonia from nitrogen and hydrogen under high temperature and pressure using an iron-based catalyst (N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3).

concepts.name: Hydrogen production from natural gas (steam reforming)
concepts.explanation: Production of H2 by reacting methane (natural gas) with steam to form CO and H2 (CH4 + H2O → CO + 3H2), often followed by water-gas shift to increase H2 yield.

concepts.name: Carbon dioxide removal in hydrogen production (gas purification)
concepts.explanation: Removal of CO2 formed during reforming/shift reactions (e.g., by chemical absorption or adsorption) to purify hydrogen feedstock for ammonia synthesis.

concepts.name: Oxidation of ammonia to nitric oxide (Ostwald process step)
concepts.explanation: Catalytic oxidation of NH3 to NO using platinum-rhodium catalyst at high temperature (4NH3 + 5O2 → 4NO + 6H2O), the first step in nitric acid manufacture.

concepts.name: Oxidation of nitrogen monoxide to nitrogen dioxide
concepts.explanation: Gas-phase oxidation of NO to NO2 (2NO + O2 → 2NO2), an intermediate step toward producing nitric acid.

concepts.name: Formation of nitric acid from NOx
concepts.explanation: Conversion of NOx gases to HNO3 typically by absorption of NO2 in water/steam to yield nitric acid and related equilibria (e.g., 3NO2 + H2O → 2HNO3 + NO).

concepts.name: Formation of ammonium nitrate (neutralization)
concepts.explanation: Production of ammonium nitrate by neutralizing nitric acid with ammonia (HNO3 + NH3 → NH4NO3), used as a fertiliser.
concepts.broader_concept: Nitric acid conversion to fertiliser products

concepts.name: Calcination: conversion of calcium carbonate to calcium oxide (CaCO3 → CaO + CO2)
concepts.explanation: Thermal decomposition (calcination) of limestone to produce quicklime (CaO) and release CO2; a key step in magnesium extraction from seawater processes.

concepts.name: Slaking: conversion of calcium oxide to calcium hydroxide (CaO + H2O → Ca(OH)2)
concepts.explanation: Hydration of quicklime to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide), used to precipitate magnesium from seawater.

concepts.name: Precipitation of magnesium hydroxide from seawater
concepts.explanation: Reaction of Mg2+ in seawater with OH- (from Ca(OH)2) to form insoluble Mg(OH)2 (Mg2+ + 2OH- → Mg(OH)2), allowing separation from solution.

concepts.name: Formation of magnesium oxide from magnesium hydroxide (calcination of Mg(OH)2 → MgO + H2O)
concepts.explanation: Thermal decomposition of precipitated magnesium hydroxide to produce magnesium oxide (MgO), a refractory material.

concepts.name: Use of urea as a fertiliser
concepts.explanation: Application and agronomic role of urea ((NH2)2CO) as a nitrogen-rich fertiliser in agriculture.

concepts.name: Use of ammonium nitrate as a fertiliser
concepts.explanation: Properties and agricultural use of ammonium nitrate (NH4NO3) as a nitrogen fertiliser produced from nitric acid and ammonia.

concepts.name: Stratospheric ozone formation and photodissociation (Chapman cycle)
concepts.explanation: UV photolysis of O2 produces O atoms which combine with O2 to form O3; O3 can be photodissociated back to O2 and O, establishing a dynamic equilibrium in the stratosphere.

concepts.name: Catalytic destruction of ozone by chlorine atoms
concepts.explanation: Chlorine atoms released in the stratosphere participate in catalytic cycles (e.g., Cl + O3 → ClO + O2; ClO + O → Cl + O2) that convert ozone to oxygen without consuming the chlorine, causing net ozone depletion.

concepts.name: CFC atmospheric stability, breakdown and chlorine release
concepts.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are very stable in the troposphere, allowing transport to the stratosphere where UV-induced breakdown releases chlorine radicals that catalyse ozone destruction; residence times are long compared with many gases.

concepts.name: Role of methane in stratospheric chlorine chemistry
concepts.explanation: Methane can react with reactive chlorine species (e.g., Cl) removing them from catalytic ozone-destruction cycles (forming HCl), thereby affecting the availability of free Cl atoms and influencing ozone depletion rates.

concepts.name: Ozone removal by nitrogen oxides (NO catalytic cycles)
concepts.explanation: NO and NO2 participate in catalytic cycles that destroy ozone (e.g., NO + O3 → NO2 + O2; NO2 + O → NO + O2), contributing to stratospheric ozone depletion.

concepts.name: Free radical chlorination of methane (formation of chloroalkanes)
concepts.explanation: Photoinitiated free radical chain reaction of methane with chlorine (initiation, propagation, termination) yields chloromethanes; this illustrates halogenation mechanisms and is the laboratory route to some chloroalkanes.

concepts.name: Greenhouse effect and major greenhouse gases
concepts.explanation: Certain atmospheric gases (notably CO2, H2O, CH4, and some halocarbons) absorb outgoing infrared radiation, trapping heat and warming the planet; different gases have differing radiative efficiencies and lifetimes.

concepts.name: Carbon dioxide dissolution and carbonate–bicarbonate equilibrium
concepts.explanation: CO2 dissolves in water forming carbonic acid which dissociates to bicarbonate and carbonate (CO2 + H2O ⇌ H2CO3 ⇌ H+ + HCO3- ⇌ 2H+ + CO3 2-); this equilibrium buffers aqueous pH and governs ocean uptake of CO2.

concepts.name: Incomplete versus complete combustion of carbon (CO and CO2 formation)
concepts.explanation: Complete combustion of carbon-rich fuels with sufficient oxygen yields CO2; limited oxygen leads to incomplete combustion producing CO (carbon monoxide) along with other products.

concepts.name: Carbon monoxide properties and toxicity
concepts.explanation: CO is a neutral oxide that binds strongly to hemoglobin, preventing oxygen transport; it is produced by incomplete combustion and is a common pollutant in smoke and vehicle exhaust.

concepts.name: Ocean uptake of atmospheric CO2 (carbon sinks)
concepts.explanation: The oceans absorb significant amounts of atmospheric CO2 via physical dissolution and subsequent chemical equilibria, acting as a sink that moderates atmospheric CO2 levels with implications for ocean chemistry.

concepts.name: Carbon cycle (atmospheric carbon exchange processes)
concepts.explanation: The carbon cycle describes the movement of carbon among atmosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and geosphere through processes such as respiration, combustion, photosynthesis, dissolution and sedimentation.

concepts.name: Nitrogen cycle and natural nitrogen fixation
concepts.explanation: The nitrogen cycle includes fixation of N2 to biologically available forms by biological organisms, lightning and industrial processes, followed by assimilation, nitrification, denitrification and return to N2.

concepts.name: Inertness of molecular nitrogen (N≡N triple bond)
concepts.explanation: Molecular nitrogen has a very strong N≡N triple bond, making it chemically unreactive under standard conditions and requiring energy-intensive or biological processes for fixation.

concepts.name: Formation of nitrogen oxides in electric discharges (lightning)
concepts.explanation: High-energy electric discharges in the atmosphere can cause N2 and O2 to react forming NO and NO2 (NOx), which are precursors to acid rain and tropospheric ozone formation.

concepts.name: Oxides of nitrogen and sulfur dissolving to form acids (acid rain)
concepts.explanation: Atmospheric NOx and SO2 can dissolve and oxidize in water to form nitric and sulfurous/sulfuric acids (e.g., SO2 → H2SO3/H2SO4, NO2 → HNO3), causing acid rain and environmental damage.
concepts.broader_concept: Atmospheric acid formation and acid rain

concepts.name: Flue gas desulfurization using limestone (scrubbing)
concepts.explanation: Industrial scrubbing removes SO2 from exhaust gases by reacting with limestone (CaCO3) or lime (CaO) to form sulfite/sulfate salts (e.g., gypsum), reducing emissions that cause acid rain.

concepts.name: Demonstration: CO2 effect on universal indicator (acidification)
concepts.explanation: Passing CO2 through water containing universal indicator turns the solution more acidic, demonstrating formation of carbonic acid and the acidifying effect of dissolved CO2.

concepts.name: Demonstration: SO2 effect on universal indicator
concepts.explanation: Introducing sulfur dioxide into water with universal indicator produces an acidic colour change, illustrating SO2 dissolution and formation of acidic species in solution.

concepts.name: Fermentation as a source of carbon dioxide (ethanol production)
concepts.explanation: Microbial fermentation of sugars (e.g., by yeast) converts glucose to ethanol and CO2 (C6H12O6 → 2 C2H5OH + 2 CO2), providing a biological source of atmospheric CO2.

concepts.name: Replacements for CFCs (HCFCs, HFCs and alternatives)
concepts.explanation: Alternatives to CFCs (such as HCFCs, HFCs and other non-ozone-depleting compounds) have been developed with shorter atmospheric lifetimes or no chlorine, reducing ozone-depletion potential though some may still be greenhouse gases.

concepts.name: Ionic crystals
concepts.explanation: Crystalline solids in which oppositely charged ions are held in a lattice by ionic (electrostatic) forces; characterized by high melting points, hardness, brittleness and electrical conductivity when molten or dissolved.

concepts.name: Covalent macromolecular crystals (giant covalent structures)
concepts.explanation: Solids in which atoms are linked in an extended network by covalent bonds (e.g., diamond, quartz) resulting in very high melting points, great hardness and generally low electrical conductivity (with known exceptions like graphite).

concepts.name: Metallic crystals
concepts.explanation: Solids composed of metal atoms in a lattice with a 'sea' of delocalised electrons (metallic bonding) leading to properties such as electrical and thermal conductivity, malleability, ductility and metallic lustre.

concepts.name: Molecular crystals
concepts.explanation: Crystalline solids made of discrete molecules held together by van der Waals forces, dipole interactions or hydrogen bonds; typically have low to moderate melting points, are softer and are poor electrical conductors.

concepts.name: X-ray crystallography (X-ray scattering to determine crystal structure)
concepts.explanation: Use of X-ray scattering/diffraction by crystals to determine the arrangement of atoms in a solid (non-mathematical understanding); includes historical contributions such as those of the Braggs and Dorothy Hodgkin.

concepts.name: Addition polymerisation of alkenes (monomers to polymers)
concepts.explanation: Polymerisation process where alkene monomers add together without elimination to form long-chain addition polymers (e.g., polyethene, poly(chloroethene), poly(phenylethene), poly(propene), poly(tetrafluoroethene)).

concepts.name: Structural differences between low-density and high-density poly(ethene)
concepts.explanation: Contrast between LDPE (branched chains causing lower density and greater flexibility) and HDPE (more linear chains, higher density, greater crystallinity and higher tensile strength/harder material).

concepts.name: Properties and uses of common addition polymers (PE, PVC, PS, PTFE, PP)
concepts.explanation: Characteristic physical properties (density, flexibility, hardness, chemical resistance) and typical industrial/domestic applications of common addition polymers: poly(ethene), poly(chloroethene, PVC), poly(phenylethene, polystyrene), poly(tetrafluoroethene, PTFE) and poly(propene).

concepts.name: Recycling of polystyrene (stages: sorting, shredding, washing, drying, re-extrusion)
concepts.explanation: Practical industrial recycling procedure for polystyrene involving sorting, shredding, washing to remove contaminants, drying and re-extrusion to form recycled material.

concepts.name: Comparison of metals and non-metals (physical properties)
concepts.explanation: Systematic comparison of typical physical properties—hardness, lustre, malleability, ductility, thermal conductivity and electrical conductivity—distinguishing metals from non-metals.

concepts.name: Alloys and effect of carbon in steel (hardness)
concepts.explanation: Concept of alloys as mixtures of metals (and sometimes non-metals); specifically how varying carbon content in iron produces steels with differing hardness and mechanical properties.

concepts.name: Galvanic (voltaic) cells and prediction of cell voltage
concepts.explanation: Construction and operation of simple cells using two different metals/electrolytes and calculation/prediction of the cell emf from electrode potentials or by using the electrochemical series.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of molten salts (general principles)
concepts.explanation: Principles and conditions for electrolysing molten ionic compounds, choice of electrodes (inert vs reactive), and use of half-equations to describe electrode processes.
concepts.broader_concept: Electrolysis procedures for molten ionic compounds
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide (laboratory experiment)
concepts.explanation: Practical electrolysis of molten PbBr2 using inert electrodes with required half-equations for electrode reactions to obtain lead and bromine.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Downs cell for sodium production
concepts.explanation: Industrial electrochemical cell (Downs cell) for producing sodium metal from molten sodium chloride, including cell design, reactions at electrodes and chlorine as a by-product.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Extraction of aluminium from bauxite (alumina electrolysis/Hall–Héroult process)
concepts.explanation: Conversion of bauxite to pure alumina followed by electrolytic reduction of alumina (dissolved in molten cryolite) to aluminium metal; key half-reactions and cell considerations.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Anodising of aluminium and properties of the oxide layer
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical formation of a protective porous aluminium oxide layer (anodising), its porous nature that permits dyeing and improved corrosion resistance.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion of metals
concepts.explanation: Electrochemical mechanisms by which metals corrode, factors affecting relative corrodability of different metals and typical products (e.g., oxides, hydroxides).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Corrosion prevention methods (galvanising, coatings, sacrificial anodes)
concepts.explanation: Practical techniques to protect metals from corrosion including protective coatings (paint, plating), galvanising iron with zinc, and using sacrificial anodes to protect structures.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Chlorine as a by-product of electrochemical extraction
concepts.explanation: Production and importance of chlorine gas arising as a by-product in electrolysis processes (e.g., sodium/chloride electrolysis) and its industrial uses.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Environmental and economic aspects of aluminium production
concepts.explanation: Environmental impacts (energy use, emissions, bauxite mining) and economic factors (need for cheap electricity) that influence aluminium production and its sustainability.
concepts.broader_concept: Sustainability and economics of metal extraction
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Contributions of Galvani, Volta, Davy and Faraday to electrochemistry
concepts.explanation: Key historical experiments and discoveries: Galvani's bioelectricity observations, Volta's voltaic pile, Davy's electrochemical isolation of metals, and Faraday's laws of electrolysis.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Transition (d-block) metals: general chemical properties
concepts.explanation: Characteristic properties of d-block elements including formation of coloured ions, multiple oxidation states, and common use as catalysts.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Variable oxidation states of transition metals
concepts.explanation: The ability of transition metals to exhibit more than one stable oxidation number and the implications for redox chemistry and compound formation.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Use of transition metals as catalysts
concepts.explanation: How transition metals and their compounds facilitate chemical reactions (heterogeneous and homogeneous catalysis) by providing alternative reaction pathways and surface-active sites.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Colours of transition metal compounds
concepts.explanation: Origin of colours in transition metal ions and complexes due to d–d electronic transitions and ligand-field effects; use in identification and analysis.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electrochemical methods for metal extraction (electrowinning and electrorefining)
concepts.explanation: Principles and applications of electrochemical extraction techniques used to obtain and purify metals from ores or impure metal (basic electrowinning and electrorefining concepts).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Blast furnace chemistry (manufacture of iron)
concepts.explanation: Chemical aspects of the blast furnace: reduction of iron oxides by carbon monoxide/coke, role of limestone in slag formation, and overall reactions producing pig iron.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Steelmaking: conversion of pig iron to steel (overview)
concepts.explanation: Main principles for producing steel from pig iron including removal of impurities, reduction of carbon content, and common industrial routes (basic overview).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Electric arc furnace process for steel manufacture (outline)
concepts.explanation: Outline of the electric arc furnace method: melting scrap/iron with electric arcs, refining steps and advantages for steel production.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Steels as alloys: composition and property relationships
concepts.explanation: Concept that steels are iron-based alloys whose mechanical and chemical properties depend on carbon content and alloying elements (e.g., strength, corrosion resistance).
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Environmental impacts of iron and steel production
concepts.explanation: Key environmental issues associated with iron and steel manufacture including CO2 emissions, air pollutants, slag and waste management, and energy consumption.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals

concepts.name: Applications of iron and steel (industrial uses)
concepts.explanation: Common uses of iron and steel in industry and everyday life (e.g., construction, transportation, machinery) and how material properties determine application.
concepts.strand: Electrochemistry and the Extraction of Metals
